<meta>Continuing from the previous page, Eusebius is interpreting the book of Micah. He previously discussed the destruction of Jerusalem and the "melting" of the old order. Now, he focuses on the positive side of the prophecy: the calling of all nations and the specific physical location of the Savior's birth in Bethlehem.</meta>

# EUSEBIUS

» [He will show] us His way, and we shall walk in His paths. For out of Zion shall go forth a law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. And He shall judge between the nations. <note>original: "ἐκ γὰρ σιὼν ἐξελεύσεται νόμος" — quoting Micah 4:2-3. Eusebius sees the "Law" no longer as the Mosaic Law, but as the Gospel spreading from Jerusalem to the world.</note> Such things concerning the calling of the nations, and the kind of meaning it holds—and how these things reached their fulfillment after the coming of our Savior—one might study again at leisure. 

Following these points, the word of prophecy begins to signal the descent of the Lord to mankind, intended for the salvation not only of the Jewish nation but of all nations. It calls out to the peoples and to everyone upon the earth, saying:
» Hear, all you peoples, and let the earth give heed, and all who are in it. And the Lord shall be a witness among us, the Lord from His holy house. And the Lord your God shall be for a testimony. <note>original: "ἀκούσατε λαοὶ πάντες... ἐξ οἴκου ἁγίου αὐτοῦ" — quoting Micah 1:2. The "holy house" is interpreted here as heaven or the divine nature.</note>

Next, the same prophet continues. Having already made declarations regarding the existence of God the Word <term>God the Word: the "Logos" or the pre-existent Christ</term> and His descent from the heavens, and having foretold the reasons for His presence among men, he then proceeds to the physical circumstances of His human life. He teaches even the specific place where He was destined to be born, saying:
» And you, Bethlehem, house of Ephrathah, are few in number to be among the thousands of Judah. Out of you shall come forth for me a leader, to be a ruler in Israel; and his goings forth are from the beginning, from the days of eternity. <note>original: "καὶ αἱ ἔξοδοι αὐτοῦ ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς ἐξ ἡμερῶν αἰῶνος" — quoting the famous prophecy in Micah 5:2.</note>

Pay careful attention to the manner in which he speaks of the one revealed in Bethlehem (this is a village in Judea). He says His "goings forth" have existed from eternity, clearly demonstrating both the pre-existence and the essence of the Ruler who came forth from Bethlehem. Now, if anyone can apply this oracle to someone else, let them show who that might be! But if it is impossible to find anyone other than our Savior Jesus Christ—who alone, after this prophecy was given, is proclaimed as having come from there—what remains but to agree that the prophecy is true, since it preserves its fulfillment for Him alone? 

Indeed, He alone of all who have ever lived is so illustrious; no other person came forth from Bethlehem after the time of the prophecy to show us the way of redemption. At the very time of His presence <note>original: "παρουσία" (parousia)</note>, the things foretold were being fulfilled. Immediately thereafter, and in a short time, the various predictions concerning the Jewish nation were met (by God's will), while the events concerning the nations followed naturally. This Savior and Lord of ours, coming from Bethlehem, was revealed as the leader of the "spiritual Israel," which is what the entire chosen and God-fearing people are now called. 

Behold how the prophet proclaims His "goings forth" as being from the divine pre-existence, from the beginning and from the days of eternity—a description that would not fit a mere human nature. Following this, the prophetic word moves down a little further and signifies the cancellation and destruction of the old legalistic religion, speaking from the perspective of the people:
» With what shall I reach the Lord? Shall I lay hold of my God Most High? If I approach Him with whole burnt offerings, with year-old calves? ... Shall I give the firstborn of my womb for the sin of my soul? <note>original: "εἰ δῶ πρωτότοκα κοιλίας μου" — quoting Micah 6:6-7. The prophet suggests that animal sacrifice and even pagan-style human sacrifice are useless for atonement.</note>

Then, speaking from the perspective of God, he gives them this answer:
» If it has been told to you, O man, what is good and what the Lord seeks from you: but to do justice and to love mercy, and to be ready to walk behind the Lord your God. <note>Micah 6:8</note>

It was necessary that these things also should come to pass under the prophesied descent of the Lord from heaven to men. At that same time, many other things were signaled: the rejection of the Jews, the rebuking of their ungodly deeds, and the destruction of their royal capital <note>Jerusalem</note>.

ΕVANGELICAL PROOF, Book 6
Page 171

...nor of the city, which was formerly celebrated among them for its perfect observance of the Mosaic law. On the contrary, [the prophecy speaks] concerning the nations: of good promises, the knowledge of God, a new law of piety, and a new Word—one that did not merely emerge from the land of the Jews, but was destined to be distributed to all the nations. # From Habakkuk.

->The Word of God was prophesied as one coming; He will come, and will not delay.<-

<margin>ʘ</margin>
And the Lord answered me, and said: Write the vision clearly on a tablet <note>original: "πυξίῳ" — literally a boxwood writing tablet, used here to emphasize the permanence and clarity of the message</note>, so that the one reading it may run <note>original: "διώκῃ" — can mean to read quickly/fluently or to run to spread the news</note>; for the vision is yet for a [set] time, and it shall rise at the end, and not in vain. If he should tarry, wait for him, because he who is coming will come and will not delay. If he should draw back, my soul has no pleasure in him; but the righteous shall live by my faith. <note>quoting Habakkuk 2:2-4</note> 

And these things explicitly announce that the one prophesied "coming, will come." And who might this be? Is it not the one declared above in the passage, "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; the Lord is God and has appeared to us"? <note>Psalm 118:26-27</note> For he says that this one, like a rising light, shall "rise at the end"—the perfect fulfillment of the ages. With this, Zechariah also agrees, saying: "Behold the man, 'Sunrise' <note>original: 'Ἀνατολὴ' — often translated as 'Branch' or 'East', but Eusebius links it to the rising sun</note> is his name, and he shall rise up from beneath him." <note>Zechariah 6:12</note> And indicating the time, the same prophet added: "at evening time there shall be light." <note>Zechariah 14:7</note> 

"If he should tarry, wait for him"; in place of this, Aquila <note>Aquila: a 2nd-century translator known for his literal Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible</note> has rendered it: "If he should linger, expect him, for coming he will come, and he will not be slow." The Epistle to the Hebrews also remembers this when it says: "Therefore do not throw away your confidence, which has a great reward. For you have need of endurance, so that when you have done the will of God, you may receive the promise. For yet a little while, and he who is coming will come and will not delay. But the righteous shall live by my faith; and if he draws back, my soul has no pleasure in him." <note>Hebrews 10:35-38</note> 

It is worth noting how the prophetic text, which is securely established in these words, has been quoted by the Apostle <note>the Apostle: Eusebius refers to the author of Hebrews as the Apostle (traditionally Paul)</note>, and how the Epistle has arranged it. In the wording of the prophecy, it says: "He who is coming will come and will not delay," and then adds, "if he should draw back, my soul has no pleasure in him." This [original order] refers somewhat loosely to receiving the "one coming" and his "not delaying," which seems awkward. For how could it be fitting to say that God has no pleasure in *him* (the Savior)? 

However, the Apostle’s distinction, by preserving the structure of the argument, clarified the meaning. For after the words, "yet a little while and he who is coming will come and will not delay," he immediately joined the phrase, "but the righteous shall live by faith." Then, he placed the phrase that appeared first in the prophecy second: "and if he draws back, my soul has no pleasure in him." 

For the Word, having once decreed through prophecy that the light promised to all nations through Christ's presence would rise late and in the evening, will not be proven false. (Indeed, instead of "not in vain," Aquila interpreted it as "it will not lie.") Then, because the presence of the one prophesied was destined to be delayed until a late and evening hour, the text encourages endurance through the words: "if he should tarry, wait for him," or "if he should linger, expect him, for coming he will come and will not delay." Thus, it urges the listener toward faith in the prediction, saying: "the righteous...

<summary>Eusebius interprets Habakkuk's prophecy of the "Vision" as a prediction of Christ's arrival, arguing that while the Savior's coming might seem delayed, it is a certain event meant for all nations. He specifically analyzes the linguistic structure of the prophecy compared to its citation in the Epistle to the Hebrews to clarify that God's "displeasure" refers to those who lose faith, not to the Savior himself.</summary>

### PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, BOOK 6 [173]

...distinctly understood as coming from "lives," derived from the singular name "life." For the word is not accented as "living creatures" <note>original: "ζώων" (*zōōn*) — accented on the first syllable, meaning animals or living beings</note>, which would be from the neuter "living thing," but it is distinctly "lives" <note>original: "ζωῶν" (*zōōn*) — accented on the second syllable, meaning of lives</note>, from the feminine plural nominative "lives." He says, therefore: "In the middle of two **lives** you shall be known." For since there is one **life** according to God, and another according to man—the one being mortal, the other eternal—the Lord reasonably passed through the experience of both. Thus, He is said to be known in the midst of two lives, according to some interpretations.

According to Aquila, however, it is not so, but rather: "as the years approach, <gloss>he says</gloss> of the living creatures." This is the same as <gloss>your work</gloss> says; and Theodotion says: "In the midst of years, give him life." And Symmachus has rendered it: "Within the years, bring him back to life." Therefore, since all of them said "give him life," it is clear that the discourse is not concerned with irrational animals, but rather with the rational Living Being <note>The "Word" or Logos</note>. For this reason, in the text of the <term>Seventy</term> <note>original: "ο'" — the Septuagint (LXX), the Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible</note> where it says, "In the midst of two lives you shall be known," although some have removed this explanation for us, we asserted that the prophetic word intended to manifest two lives: one being the divine, and the other the human.

To these words the prophet adds:
> **"In my soul being troubled in wrath, you will remember mercy."**

This teaches that when he beheld the time of the prophesied Passion in the Spirit, he was deeply disturbed. Nevertheless, he says that at this very time in which his soul was troubled—though wrath was never divided or contested among men because of the impieties dared against the Lord—the philanthropic Lord remembered mercy for them instead of wrath, just as a son might receive from a good father. Indeed, His Passion became the cause of salvation and mercy, according to God, for the whole world.

To these things is added:
> **"God will come from Teman."**

The word "Teman" is translated into the Greek language as "completion." Thus, it makes no difference if it were plainly said: "God will come at the completion." For it was at the completion of the age <note>The "end of the world" or the culmination of history</note> and in these last days that the beneficence of the God of all appeared to us through our Savior. Perhaps he also prophesies His second and glorious arrival in these words, so that the phrase "God will come from Teman" should be read from a different starting point, as Him coming at the completion of the age. [Teman also refers to] the southern parts of Israel; for Teman is translated as "the south." Hence, Theodotion, translating this passage, says: "God will come from the south."

What follows—**"and the Holy One from the overshadowed, thick mountain"**—you will understand by comparing the words found in Zechariah: "I saw by night, and behold, a man riding upon a red horse, and he stood between the overshadowed mountains." I believe that this one riding the red horse and standing between the overshadowed mountains is the same one manifested in the prophecy currently at hand, which says that the Holy One will come from the "overshadowed, thick mountain." In both cases, "overshadowed mountains" are mentioned. I believe this refers to the Paradise of God, which He planted in Eden toward the east, or even the heavenly Jerusalem. For "mountains are round about her, and the Lord is round about His people." These are called "overshadowed" because they are full of divine powers and holy spirits, as if they were lush and densely wooded. But while in Zechariah a man riding a red horse is clearly seen by him—the name signifying the incarnation and the flesh of our Savior—here He is named "Lord" and "Holy One." For He made His arrival from God to men, and from the more divine regions...

### From Zechariah.

-> How the Lord Almighty confesses that He was sent by another Lord Almighty <-
-> for the destruction of the wicked. <-

<margin>>></margin> **Thus says the Lord Almighty: After the glory he has sent me to the nations that plundered you. For he who touches you is as one who touches the apple of his eye. For behold, I bring my hand upon them, and they shall be spoils for those who served them, and you shall know that the Lord Almighty has sent me.** In these verses, the Lord Almighty Himself says that He has been sent, and He teaches who the one who sent Him is, saying: **And you shall know that the Lord Almighty has sent me.** From this you clearly have two persons using the same title: the Lord Almighty who sends, and the one being sent who shares the same name as the sender. Whom else could you say is the one being sent, other than the God-Word <note>original: "θεὸν λόγον" (*theon logon*)</note> who has been proclaimed to us through many passages, who confesses that He has been sent by the Father? He clearly stated: **After the glory he has sent me.** This indicates that while He was in the glory that is with the Father, He was afterward sent **to the nations that plundered you.** For when the Word of God was sent, He brought under His own authority those nations that were formerly enemies and hostile to the people of God; He "plundered" them through His disciples, who were themselves a part of the people of the <term>circumcision</term> <note>The Jewish people</note>. These nations had long been enslaved by those from whom He set them free. For just as those nations once turned the people of God away from their ancestral piety and made them "spoils" for their own demons, so too will those nations one day be plundered from their ancestral idolatry by those they once enslaved, and they will be transferred under the yoke of **Hebrew piety**. The Lord says that this will happen through Him, since He was sent by the Father for such a great achievement. One might also mention certain intelligible and invisible powers...

You will observe that it again declares the reason for His arrival in the words: **And many nations shall flee to the Lord for refuge in that day, and shall be His people.** The Word <note>The Logos/Christ</note> announces these "glad tidings" to the "daughter of Zion." He addresses the Church of God in this way because she is considered the daughter of the **heavenly Jerusalem**, which the holy Apostle <note>St. Paul, in Galatians 4:26.</note> calls the "mother of the saints." Or, quite clearly, the Church might be called the "daughter of Zion" because she was established from the former "synagogue of the circumcision" through the apostles and evangelists. This daughter would be the Church gathered from the nations, reckoned in the place of the former daughter through the apostles of our Savior.

» ...His name shall be one, encircling all the earth and the desert. <note>original: "ὄνομα αὐτῷ ἕν, κυκλοῦν πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν ἔρημον"</note> Truly, since the prophecy declared that the nation of the Jews would suffer such things in the days of the Lord, who would not marvel at the outcome? For at the same time that those of the circumcision <note>A common term for the Jewish people in early Christian writing.</note> set themselves against our Savior and Lord, Jesus Christ, all the godless things predicted for them reached their fulfillment five hundred years after the prophecy. This began with Pilate and continued until the sieges of Nero, Titus, and Vespasian, through a series of incessant and overlapping calamities, as anyone can read in the *History* written by Flavius Josephus. Thus, it was likely that **half of the city** perished in that siege, just as the prophecy says. But not long after, during the time of the Emperor Hadrian, when another Jewish uprising occurred, the **remaining half of the city** was besieged and driven out once more. Since that time and until today, the place has become entirely inaccessible to them.

Now, if anyone should claim that these things were fulfilled during the time of Antiochus Epiphanes <note>A Seleucid king (175–164 BC) who famously persecuted the Jews, leading to the Maccabean Revolt. Eusebius is arguing against this common alternative interpretation.</note>, let him consider whether he is able to apply the rest of the prophecy to the times of Antiochus. For instance: were the people taken captive in that specific way? Did the **feet of the Lord stand upon the Mount of Olives**? Did the Lord become **King over all the earth** in that day? And did one name of the Lord encircle all the earth and the desert at a time when Antiochus himself only ruled over Syria? How could anyone apply the rest of the prediction to the reign of Antiochus?

But in our interpretation, these things are fulfilled both literally and according to a deeper spiritual meaning. For at the presence of Jesus Christ in Jerusalem, their city—this very Jerusalem and its entire system and constitution of worship according to the Law of Moses—was abolished. Immediately, they suffered a spiritual captivity instead of a physical one, because they did not receive the Savior and Redeemer of human souls, who came to proclaim release to those held captive by evil demons and recovery of sight to those who were blind in their understanding. Because they suffered these things due to their unbelief, those who recognized their Redeemer—his own disciples and apostles, and many others from the circumcision who believed in Him—became what the Apostle Paul calls "a remnant according to the election of grace." <note>A reference to Romans 11:5.</note> As he says:

> » And if the Lord of Sabaoth <note>A Hebrew title meaning "Lord of Hosts" or "Lord of Armies."</note> had not left us a seed, we would have become like Sodom, and been made like Gomorrah. <note>Quoting Romans 9:29, which cites Isaiah 1:9.</note>

Having understood this spiritual siege, they were preserved not only from the literal siege but from the physical destruction that followed. Indeed, the apostles and disciples of our Savior, and all those from the Jews who believed in Him, traveled far from the land of Judea and were scattered among the other nations. They were thus able to escape the destruction that then fell upon their native city. The prophecy anticipated this and decreed it through the words: » **but the rest of my people shall not be utterly destroyed.** Following this, it adds:

> » The Lord shall go forth and take His stand among those nations, just as in the day of His arraying in the day of battle. <note>original: "ἐξελεύσεται κύριος καὶ παρατάξεται ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἐκείνοις"</note>

Among which nations would the Lord take His stand, if not those who besieged Jerusalem? This word reveals that the Lord Himself would fight alongside the besiegers, being present among them and arrayed with them like a general and a champion, while they campaigned against Jerusalem. For the word does not say...

# THE PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, Book 6.

<margin>»</margin> ...his name in a circle throughout all the earth and the desert. But indeed, the Jewish nation was to suffer such things in the "days of the Lord," as the prophecy declared; who then would not marvel at the resulting outcome? # EVANGELICAL PROOF, Book 6

» ...his name in a circle around all the earth and the desert. <note>This completes the quotation of Zechariah 14:9 from the previous page.</note> Since the prophecy declared that the Jewish nation would suffer such things in the days of the Lord, who would not marvel at the result of this manifestation? For at the same time as faith in our Savior and Lord arose, those of the circumcision <note>The Jewish people</note> acted impiously toward him. Consequently, all the parts of their religion were godlessly brought to an end five hundred years after the prophecy was given—starting from the time of Pilate, and continuing until the sieges of Nero, Titus, and Vespasian. One who is unbridled <note>original: "ἀχαλινοί" (akhalinoi); suggesting those with an unquenchable thirst for detail</note> in the face of these failures and successive disasters may read of them in the history written by Flavius Josephus <note>A first-century Romano-Jewish historian whose works provide the primary account of the destruction of Jerusalem</note>. At that time, it is likely that "half of the city" perished in the siege, just as the prophecy says. But not long afterward, under the Emperor Hadrian, when another Jewish uprising occurred, the remaining "half" of the city was besieged and driven out once again. Since that time, the place has remained entirely barred and inaccessible to them until this very day.

If someone should claim that these things were fulfilled during the time of Antiochus <note>Antiochus IV Epiphanes, the Seleucid king who desecrated the Temple in the 2nd century BC</note>, let them consider whether they are able to apply the rest of the prophecy to those same times: was the people truly taken into such a captivity then? Did the feet of the Lord stand upon the Mount of Olives? Did the Lord become King over all the earth in that day? And did the one name of the Lord encircle all the earth and the desert when Antiochus of Syria was in power? How could anyone apply the rest of the prophecy’s fulfillment to the reign of Antiochus?

In our view, however, these things have been fulfilled literally, but also according to a different understanding <note>original: "κατ' ἑτέραν δὲ διάνοιαν" (kat’ heteran de dianoian); referring to an allegorical or spiritual interpretation</note>. For after the coming of our Savior and Lord, the Christ, their city—Jerusalem itself—and its entire system and constitution of worship according to the Law of Moses were destroyed. Immediately, they suffered an "intellectual" <note>or spiritual</note> captivity in addition to the physical one, by not receiving the Savior and Redeemer of human souls, who came to preach "release to the captives" held by evil demons, and "recovery of sight" to those blind in their minds. While those people suffered these things because of their unbelief, those who recognized their Redeemer—namely his personal disciples, apostles, and evangelists, as well as the great multitudes of the circumcision who believed in him—were saved. As the Apostle says:

» "So then also at this time there is a remnant according to the election of grace." <note>Romans 11:5</note>
» "And unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we would have become like Sodom, and been made like Gomorrah." <note>Isaiah 1:9, quoted in Romans 9:29</note>

This "remnant" was preserved through the metaphorical siege in an infinite way; and not only that, but they were preserved during the literal fulfillment as well. For the apostles and disciples of our Savior, and all those of Jewish descent who believed in him, were far away from the land of Judea and were scattered among the rest of the nations; thus they were able to escape the destruction that then fell upon the inhabitants of the city. The prophecy anticipated this and decreed it by saying: "But the rest of my people shall not be utterly destroyed." Immediately after this, it adds:

» "And the Lord shall go forth and shall draw up his battle lines among those nations, just as on his day of battle in the day of war." <note>Zechariah 14:3</note>

Among which nations will the Lord draw up his lines, if not those who besieged Jerusalem? The text indicates that the Lord himself would fight alongside the besiegers, being present among them and campaigning with them like a general and their champion as they marched against Jerusalem. For the Word does not say...

# EUSEBIUS: EVANGELICAL PROOF

<meta>catchword: Acts</meta>

...the Lord, and he shall be set apart for the nations. He also speaks specifically concerning Jerusalem and its inhabitants, of whom the discourse here treats. But when it says, **"and his feet shall stand in that day upon the Mount of Olives, which is opposite Jerusalem, to the east,"** <note>Zechariah 14:4</note> what else does this manifest but the Lord God—the Divine Word <note>original: "θεὸν λόγον" (theon logon); a title for Christ as the eternal Reason or Word of God</note> himself—and the standing and establishment of his Church? Why is it that the "Mount of Olives" is specifically named and emphasized in the present passage? 

Just as the "trampled one" <note>The old Israel</note> was called a vineyard, and the House of Israel was declared to be the "vineyard of the Lord of Sabaoth," and the "beloved new plant" was the vine of Judah; so, following the same spiritual interpretation, you might say that the Church gathered from the nations was called the **"Mount of Olives"** by the Master. This Church, which was once a wild olive tree, he planted by grafting it into the apostolic roots of the cultivated olive tree after the original branches were cut away. This is exactly what the Apostle <note>Saint Paul in Romans 11:17–24</note> teaches us. He planted it as his own, almost as if saying through the prophecy: **"The Lord called your name a fair olive tree, leafy and beautiful."** <note>Jeremiah 11:16</note>

For since the wise Vineyard, which was meant to produce grapes, instead produced thorns—not righteousness, but a cry of distress—God naturally handed over its fence and its wall to enemies to be plundered and trampled, according to the prophecy of Isaiah. <note>Isaiah 5:1–7</note> He then established another field for himself, the one called by us at this present time, because it obtained mercy and was planted with the unfading plants of Christ—that is, with holy souls nourished by light. Of such a soul it is said: **"But I am like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God."** <note>Psalm 52:8</note>

As for the statement that the Mount of Olives is **"opposite Jerusalem"**: this is because the old, earthly Jerusalem and the worship within it were replaced by the dissolution of that old city. When the Word said earlier concerning Jerusalem that **"the city shall be taken, and the hostile and warring nations shall be gathered against it, and its spoils shall be divided,"** <note>Zechariah 14:2</note> it naturally follows that the Lord's feet would not stand *in* Jerusalem. For how could they, once it was destroyed? Instead, the prophecy teaches that he would move from there to the mountain directly across from Jerusalem, the one called "of Olives," where he shall stand. 

The prophet Ezekiel also foresaw this long ago in the Spirit. He says: **"And the cherubim lifted up their wings, and the wheels were beside them; and the glory of the God of Israel was over them, above them. And the glory of the Lord went up from the midst of the city and stood upon the mountain which was opposite the city."** <note>Ezekiel 11:22–23</note>

In another sense, one can see this fulfilled literally even today. All those who have believed in Christ run together from all parts of the earth, not as they used to do in ancient times to see the splendor of Jerusalem, or to worship in the sanctuary that once stood there. Rather, they come to witness the history and the clear proof of the prophecy: the desolation of Jerusalem and the worship on the Mount of Olives which stands opposite it. For it was there that the glory of the Lord moved after leaving the former city. 

Furthermore, according to the literal and historical account, the feet of our Lord and Savior—the Word himself, through whom he conversed with men while dwelling in a human tabernacle—truly stood upon the Mount of Olives. It was at the cave that is shown there that he prayed; it was on the summit of the Mount of Olives that he revealed the mysteries concerning the end of the world to his disciples; and it was from that very spot that he made his ascent into heaven, as Luke tells us in the **Acts** <note>Acts 1:9–12</note>...

<summary>Eusebius interprets the Mount of Olives as a symbol for the Church and explains why God's presence moved there from the old Jerusalem. He cites the literal fulfillment of this prophecy through Christ’s teachings and his Ascension from the mountain.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Eusebius’s commentary on the prophecy of Zechariah regarding the Mount of Olives. Having established the mountain as a symbol for the Church, he now cites the Book of Acts to link the physical location to the Ascension of Christ and provides a spiritual interpretation of the mountain "splitting" into four directions.</meta>

->### EVANGELICAL PROOF, Book 6###<-

> „ ...the **Acts of the Apostles** teaches this, saying: 'While they were looking on, he was lifted up, and a cloud took him out of their sight. And while they were gazing into heaven as he went, behold, two men stood by them in white robes, who also said, "Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven."' To which he <note>The author of Acts, Luke</note> adds: 'Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem.'</quote> <note>Acts 1:9–12</note>

Indeed, according to the literal word, the Mount of Olives is "opposite Jerusalem," being the mountain that lies to its east. However, according to its deeper meaning <term>dianoia: the spiritual or underlying intent of a text</term>, it is the **Holy Church of Christ**, the mountain upon which she is founded. Concerning this, the Savior teaches:

> „ **"A city set on a hill cannot be hidden."** <note>Matthew 5:14</note>

This Church has been raised up in place of the fallen Jerusalem which did not rise again, and it is "trodden by the feet of the Lord." It is not only "opposite Jerusalem," but also "to the east" of it, having received the first rays of the light of godliness. It has become far superior to the old Jerusalem, drawing near to the **Sun of Righteousness** itself, of whom it has been said:

> „ **"But for you who fear my name, the Sun of Righteousness shall rise."** <note>Malachi 4:2</note>

The text follows by saying that the Mount of Olives shall be split—half of it toward the east and the sea <note>The "sea" refers to the West/Mediterranean</note>, a very great chasm <note>original: "χάος μέγα" (chaos mega); often translated as "valley" in biblical contexts, but Eusebius emphasizes the scale of the division</note>, and half of it shall tilt toward the north and half toward the south. This can signify the expansion of the Church throughout the whole inhabited world. It fills the "east," representing the eastern nations and the dawn. It extends even to the "western sea" and the islands within it. Furthermore, it has reached the "south" and the "meridian," as well as the "north" and the "arctic." For everywhere, the Church—this "valley" of the Lord mentioned in the prophecy—has been victoriously planted.

One can also interpret this "splitting" of the Church of Christ as an allusion to the schisms and **heresies** that have occurred and continue to occur, as well as the falls in morals and lifestyle. For the prophecy says the mountain shall be divided into two, then into four parts: half toward the east, half toward the sea (a very great chasm), half toward the north, and half toward the south. Thus, it is divided into four parts: two of these are more venerable and better, while two are their opposites. 

Consider whether, through these, the "east" and the "south" signify the two ranks of those who have attained progress in God. One rank consists of those perfected in knowledge, reason, and the other gifts of the Divine Spirit; the other consists of those who live uprightly and persevere in blessings. The remaining two parts, separated from the former, would be the "sea" and the "north," both signifying a leaning toward wickedness. For it is said:

> „ **"From the north, evil shall flare up upon all the inhabitants of the land."** <note>Jeremiah 1:14</note>

And it says the "dragon" makes its dwelling in the "sea." <note>Cf. Isaiah 27:1</note> Therefore, it is fitting that here, too, two types of those who fall away from the Church are shown: those who sin in matters of knowledge <note>Heresy</note> and those who sin in their character <note>Immorality</note>. These are the divisions of the symbolic Mount of Olives hinted at by the prophecy. Following these things, it is added:

> „ **"And the valley of my mountains shall be blocked up, and the valley of the mountains shall be joined as far as Azal; and it shall be blocked up as it was blocked up in the face of the earthquake in the days of Uzziah, King of [Judah]."** <note>Zechariah 14:5</note>

<summary>Eusebius interprets the splitting of the Mount of Olives in Zechariah's prophecy as a dual metaphor for the Church’s global expansion and the internal divisions caused by heresy and moral failure.</summary>

Now, he addresses the "valley" mentioned in the prophecy, linking it to the end of traditional Jewish temple worship and citing historical accounts of a great earthquake during the reign of King Uzziah to illustrate his point.</meta>

->### EUSEBIUS
#### EVANGELICAL PROOF, Book 6####<-

<margin>”</margin>...of the King of Judah. The "valley" among these mountains of God would be the physical and Jewish worship that was performed long ago in Jerusalem according to the 
<margin>”</margin>Law of Moses. This present word <note>The prophecy of Zechariah</note> prophesies that this valley will be shut off—as if blocked up—
<margin>”</margin>saying: **"And the valley of my mountains shall be closed, and the ravine of the mountains shall be joined as far as Asael,** <note>original: *Asael*. This is a Greek transliteration of a Hebrew place name often rendered as 'Azel' in English Bibles.</note> **and it shall be closed."** 
<margin>”</margin>In place of this, the translator Symmachus <note>A 2nd-century translator of the Old Testament into Greek</note> has written: **"And the valley of my mountains shall be closed, and the valley of the mountains shall still be equal to the adjacent part, and it shall be closed."** Through these words, he presents the reason for the 
<margin>”</margin>blocked valley. It is the valley of God, because it has been granted to draw near to that which is adjacent to it. 
<margin>”</margin>This "adjacent part" was the Mountain of the Lord, named according to its spiritual meaning <note>original: *psyche* (soul/inner meaning)</note>, which he called **Asael**, following the version of the Seventy <note>The Septuagint, the standard Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible</note>. 
<margin>”</margin>According to the Hebrew tongue, this name signifies **"The Work of God."** <note>Hebrew: *Asa-El*</note> Thus, he says, the old valley—having approached the Mountain and the Church of God, which is the "Work of God"—will be blocked and shut off, 
<margin>”</margin>in the same way it was blocked **"before the face of the earthquake in the days of Uzziah, King of Judah."** 

Seeking within myself and searching the Divine Scriptures to see if ever in the days of Uzziah the valley described here was physically blocked by an earthquake, I could find nothing in the histories of the **Books of Kings**. There is no record there of a physical earthquake occurring in his time, nor is any such event concerning a valley written down. It is recorded that Uzziah was righteous at first, but later fell away when his mind became proud, and because of this, he attempted to offer incense <note>A ritual reserved only for priests</note> contrary to the established laws. For this reason, **leprosy** broke out upon his face. These things are contained in the Books of Kings. 

However, **Josephus**—who accurately recorded the external Jewish traditions <term>deuteroseis: secondary or oral traditions that supplement the biblical text</term>, being a "Hebrew of Hebrews" and reporting what he heard from his ancestors' generations—explains these times. 
<margin>”</margin>He says that when the priests were urging Uzziah to leave the Temple and not to usurp the things belonging to God, 
<margin>”</margin>Uzziah became angry and threatened them with death unless they kept quiet. At that moment, an earthquake 
<margin>”</margin>shook the earth. As the Temple split open, a brilliant light flashed out and fell upon 
<margin>”</margin>the King’s face, so that leprosy immediately rushed over him. 
<margin>”</margin>Furthermore, in front of the city at the place called **Eroge**, half of the mountain toward the west broke off 
<margin>”</margin>and rolled four stadia <note>roughly half a mile or 800 meters</note> toward the eastern mountain and stopped there, so that the 
<margin>”</margin>roads were blocked, as were the royal gardens. 

Let these details from the writings of Josephus’s *Jewish Antiquities* be set down here. For in searching the prophet **Amos**, I found at the beginning of his prophecy that he began to prophesy **"in the days of Uzziah, King of Judah, two years before the earthquake."** But he did not clearly explain which earthquake he meant. I believe the same prophet describes this earthquake further on, where he says: 
<margin>”</margin>**"I saw the Lord standing upon the altar, and he said: 'Smite the altar, and the gateposts shall be shaken. And cut into the heads of** 
<margin>”</margin>**all of them, and the remnant of them I will kill with the sword.'"** 

Through these words, the "earthquake" may be said to represent the pulling down of the formerly sacred things of the Jewish nation and the worship they performed in Jerusalem. It also represents the destruction that overtook them after the coming of our Savior. At that time, when they tried to hide the Christ of God—who is the true High Priest—leprosy broke out in their souls, just as I previously mentioned regarding Uzziah. It was then that, by an invisible power, the Lord himself...

<summary>Eusebius uses Josephus's account of a miraculous earthquake and Uzziah's leprosy to interpret Zechariah's prophecy as the spiritual "blocking" of old Jewish rituals in favor of the Church.</summary>

This is meant both according to the **literal word**, regarding the Roman siege—during which I believe such events occurred—and also according to the **spiritual meaning** <note>original: *dianoian*</note>, when the physical and lowlier worship of the Law of Moses was shut off, so as to be no longer active. This was due to the "earthquake" that prophetically came upon the Jewish nation from that time, and because of the other things that have been recorded. And see if he does not most clearly indicate the day of our Savior's Passion. On that day, the phrase **"there shall be no light"** was fulfilled when, from the sixth hour, darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour. <note>Matthew 27:45</note> The phrase **"but cold and frost"** occurred when, according to Luke, those who arrested Jesus led Him to the house of the high priest. Peter followed at a distance, and when they had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard, he sat among the others to warm himself. <note>Luke 22:54–55</note> John, on the other hand, explicitly mentioned the cold, saying: <margin>»</margin> **"The servants and officers stood there, having made a charcoal fire, because it was cold, and they were warming themselves."** <note>John 18:18; original: *psychos* (cold/chill)</note> He says: **"That same day shall be known to the Lord,"** yet it is **"not day and not night."** It was "not day" because of the previous statement, "there shall be no light," which was fulfilled when darkness fell from the sixth to the ninth hour. But it was "not night" either, because of the addition, **"toward evening there shall be light,"** which was also accomplished when, after the ninth hour, the day regained its usual light. 

These things were also fulfilled according to the **spiritual meaning**. Generally, for the Jewish nation, after their bold crime against Christ, darkness, frost, and cold occurred because their minds were darkened so that the light of the Gospel did not shine in their hearts, and their love for God grew cold. Conversely, "toward evening," the light of the knowledge of Christ dawned, so that those who formerly sat in darkness and the shadow of death saw a "great light," according to the voices of Isaiah. On that very day of the Lord, he says: <margin>»</margin> **"Living water shall go out from Jerusalem."** <note>Zechariah 14:8</note> This was the rational and drinkable, life-giving and saving drink of Christ's teaching, about which He Himself spoke in the Gospel according to John...

The reason for His journey there is as follows: Since it is remembered that the error of idolatry first began in Egypt, and the Egyptians were thought to be the most superstitious of all men, and were furthermore enemies and foes to the people of God, having stood at the greatest distance from the prophets, it was fitting that the power of God should visit them first. For this reason, the message of His Gospel teaching has overcome the strength of the Egyptians more than that of any other people. Therefore, the present prophecy declares that the Lord would journey there again, but would no longer come to the Jewish land, nor would He come to Jerusalem to worship there, nor would He be worshipped by the Jews according to the things ordained through Moses, nor would He offer sacrifices on the altar in Jerusalem. Instead, the prophecy says that none of these things would happen, but that the Lord Himself would visit the Egyptians and deem the people worthy of His providence, making them worthy of great blessings. This journey, then, would set things right, which is confirmed as having been fulfilled by the very deeds that followed the appearance of our Savior Jesus Christ. For as they say, the foul and wicked demons who formerly inhabited Egypt, lurking in the **cult-statues** <note>original: ξοάνοις; ancient wooden or stone images of gods.</note> for a long age and enslaving the souls of the Egyptians with every error of superstition, immediately were stirred up when they perceived a certain stranger and divine power visiting them. Feeling a shudder within themselves, their heart and intellectual power was defeated within them, retreating and being conquered by the power that invisibly drove them out and, like a fire, scorched them with an unutterable word. But at that time the demons suffered these things invisibly upon the journey of our Savior Jesus Christ into Egypt in the flesh. However, when afterwards the Gospel concerning Him was openly preached to the Egyptians, just as to the rest of the nations, His invisible power journeyed with His apostles—secretly accompanying them, working with them, and proclaiming through them His pious teaching, commanding them to worship only the one and only true God, and turning them away from the demons that had long ago led them astray. From that point on, a strife and civil war arose among the Egyptians, just as among the rest of the nations: some withdrew from the error of polytheism and ran toward the Word of the Christ of God, while others fought against these people from the opposite side, being driven to frenzy by their own demons, so that even brothers were divided against each other and the dearest friends came to blows with swords because of the teaching of Christ. # PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, Book 6

...and the Savior Himself confirmed this prophetic prediction, saying in the Gospels:
> "Brother will deliver brother to death, and a father his child; and children will rise up against parents and put them to death." And again: "Do not think that I have come to bring peace to the earth; I did not come to bring peace, but a sword. For from now on there will be five in one house divided, three against two and two against three. They will be divided: father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law." <note>A combination of Matthew 10:21, 34 and Luke 12:52–53. Eusebius uses these to show that Christ’s arrival brings a "holy division" between those who believe and those who cling to old ways.</note>

For these words must be referred to the prophetic voice, which says regarding the presence of the Lord in Egypt: "Egyptian shall be stirred up against Egyptian, and a man shall fight against his brother." Indeed, the law of the New Covenant of Christ was raised up against the law of polytheistic superstition, when the law of Christ, fighting through His teaching, battled the idolatry of the nations. Thus, the city and the way of life found in the Church of Christ fought against the polytheistic laws of the unbelieving nations. Therefore it is said, "city against city, and law against law." <note>original: "πόλις ἐπὶ πόλιν, καὶ νόμος ἐπὶ νόμον" — quoting Isaiah 19:2.</note> Moreover, regarding these Egyptians, all their idolatry and the spirit of idolatry at work within them shall be shaken; for it says that their "handmade objects" <note>An ancient term for idols.</note> are shaken even now. Though they wish to do many things against the teaching of Christ, as if to quench it and make it vanish from among men, their counsel shall be scattered by God, as the prophecy says:
> "And the spirit of the Egyptians shall be troubled within them, and I will scatter their counsel."

And though they learn and inquire about many things against us through oracles and divinations from their gods and the demons lurking in their statues, as well as from those who long ago terrified them as ventriloquists, they gain nothing more from them. <term>ventriloquists</term> <note>original: "γαστριμύθους" (gastrimythous) — literally "belly-speakers." In antiquity, this referred to mediums or necromancers believed to have a spirit speaking from within them, like the Witch of Endor.</note> Therefore the Word says: "And they shall consult their gods and their statues, and those who speak from the earth."

For he says that those who flee for refuge to their fabricated gods will find no benefit or help, especially when the Lord delivers them over to "harsh lords and kings." This occurred when they, obeying their demons and being energized by them, stirred up persecutions against the Church of God. Furthermore, consider how, until the appearance of our Savior Jesus Christ, all of Egypt enjoyed its own native kings and lived in autonomy and prosperity. The dynasty of Egypt was ancient, long-lasting, and highly revered. But from the time of the Roman Augustus—during whose reign our Lord was born—when he subdued Egypt after the capture of Cleopatra, the last of the Ptolemies, they have fallen under the authority of the Romans. <note>Cleopatra VII was the final ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom; her defeat in 30 BCE turned Egypt into a Roman province.</note> They are governed by Roman laws and decrees, having been deprived of their former autonomy and prosperity. Thus, in this too, the prophetic oracle is proven true, speaking of the governors and leaders sent out to oversee these labors, and of the rest of the local officials, saying:
> "And I will deliver Egypt into the hands of men who are harsh lords."

Regarding those who administer the government as a whole, and what follows: instead of this, Aquila says, "and a mighty king shall rule over them." <note>Aquila of Sinope was a 2nd-century translator of the Hebrew Bible into Greek, known for his literalism.</note> And Symmachus says, "and a strong king shall have authority over them." <note>Symmachus the Ebionite was another translator whose Greek version was praised for its elegance.</note> In this way, I believe the Roman Empire is named, by which—as if by a bridle and a bond—not only the Egyptians (the most superstitious of all men) are fettered, but also...

And here, the arrival of God is explicitly announced as bringing salvation and being the cause of many good things. For a healing is clearly indicated—the recovery of sight for the blind, and furthermore, a cure for the lame and those whose tongues are tied. These things achieved their fulfillment in no other way than through the presence of our Savior, Jesus Christ, by whom the eyes of the blind were opened and the deaf regained their hearing. What need is there to mention how many blind, deaf, and lame people recovered their natural functions through His disciples? It is evident that countless people, worn down by various diseases and infirmities, were deemed worthy of healing and salvation by Him, according to the divine prophetic prediction, or rather, according to the truth found in the testimony of the Holy Gospels. 

In these passages, the Word riddles <note>Eusebius often uses "the Word" (Logos) to refer to the divine voice of Scripture or Christ Himself speaking through the prophets.</note> the "desert" as the Church of the Nations, which was anciently a desert void of God, and it is for this company that the good news is proclaimed. And the Word says that, among other things, "the glory of Lebanon" will be given to this desert. Now, it is a figurative way of speaking to call Jerusalem "Lebanon," as we shall demonstrate in due time through proofs from the Holy Scripture. Therefore, the present prophecy teaches that during the presence of God among men, the "glory of Lebanon" would be given to the aforementioned "desert"—I mean, the Church of the Nations. 

Regarding the phrase, "and the honor of Carmel," Aquila <note>A 2nd-century translator known for his literal, sometimes strained, Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible.</note> says: *the comeliness of Carmel and Sharon, they shall see the glory of the Lord.* Symmachus <note>An ebionite translator of the late 2nd century whose Greek style was more idiomatic than Aquila's.</note> says: *the beauty of Carmel and the plain, they shall see the glory of the Lord.* And Theodotion <note>A Hellenistic Jewish scholar who revised earlier Greek translations to better match the Hebrew text.</note> says: *the loveliness of Carmel and Sharon, they shall see the glory of the Lord.* 

By these names, I believe the prophecy riddles that it is not Jerusalem, nor Judea, but the land of the nations that will be deemed worthy of the knowledge of God. For Carmel, and the place called Sharon, were regions belonging to foreign nations. This, then, is the literal meaning. But the spiritual sense <note>original: "διάνοια" — the deeper or intended meaning beyond the literal text.</note> is that even today, those who were previously blinded in their souls—as if they were wood or stone—and the rest...

He argues that the physical healings performed by Christ and His disciples prove the divine nature of this transition from spiritual barrenness to the knowledge of God.</summary>

» ...proclaiming good things, for I will make your salvation heard, saying, "Zion, your God shall reign." Following these things, the prophecy about the passion of Christ is joined under one and the same sequence, because we shall not be without it. Being one and the same Lord who said in the previous section to the Jewish people: "For your sins you were sold, and for your lawlessness I sent away your mother; because I came, and there was no man; I called, and there was no one who obeyed" <note>Isaiah 50:1-2</note>. Therefore, by my hand He says to the same people: "Because of you my name is blasphemed among the nations." Then, as if returning to the same people, He adds: "Therefore my people shall know my name." He teaches that it is not another, but the same Lord who spoke in the prophets, who once visited this life <note>referring to the Incarnation</note>, saying: "I am He; I who speak am present." 

Now the phrase, "How beautiful upon the mountains, like the feet of one proclaiming the news of peace, like one proclaiming good things, I will make your salvation heard, saying, 'Zion, your God shall reign,'" the others have rendered more clearly in translation. <note>Eusebius is comparing the standard Greek Septuagint translation with other 2nd-century Greek versions by Aquila and Symmachus.</note>

Aquila, for instance, saying: "How beautiful upon the mountains were the feet of the messenger, making peace heard, proclaiming good, making salvation heard, saying to Zion, 'Your God has reigned.'" 

And Symmachus saying: "How comely upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger, making peace audible, proclaiming good things, making salvation audible, saying to Zion, 'Your God has reigned.'"

And the phrase: "The voice of those guarding you was raised, and with the voice they shall rejoice together, for they shall see eye to eye." Symmachus translated it this way: "The voice of your watchmen, they lifted up their voice, for they shall praise together. For they shall see face to face." 

In these words, "watchmen" <note>original: σκοποί (skopoi)</note> would refer to the holy Apostles of our Savior, who, having seen the one prophesied face to face, lifted up their voice, preaching to the whole world. The Apostle [Paul] knows a heavenly Zion and Jerusalem in these places of the messenger, through which he says: "But the Jerusalem above is free, which is our mother" <note>Galatians 4:26</note>; and, "You have come to Mount Zion and the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of angels in festal gathering" <note>Hebrews 12:22</note>. 

Moreover, the Church established through Christ in every place on earth might be called Zion, as well as Jerusalem—the pious establishment which formerly existed only among the Jews of old, but was turned into a desert because of their impieties. Then it again obtained a renewal for the better through the manifestation of our Savior. Therefore the prophecy says: "Let the desert places of Jerusalem break forth into joy together, for the Lord has had mercy on her and has delivered Jerusalem." 

Zion and Jerusalem are both used for the holy and God-loving soul. Insofar as it is elevated in life, having its citizenship in heaven and contemplating things beyond this world, he calls it Zion—for the name is translated as "watchtower" <note>original: σκοπευτήριον (skopeutērion)</note>. Insofar as it is established in stability and calm, he calls it Jerusalem—for the name signifies "vision of peace" <note>original: ὅρασιν εἰρήνης (horasin eirēnēs)</note>. # PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, Book 6

» The calling of God is most clearly shown through the phrase: "And the Lord God will reveal His holy arm before all the nations, and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation from our God." <note>Isaiah 52:10</note> You should consider the **arm of God** to be no other than the **Word** <note>original: "Logos"</note> and the **Wisdom**, or the Lord Himself, who is the Christ of God. 

This is easily demonstrated from many sources. Indeed, in the book of Exodus, it was necessary for Israel to be rescued from their slavery under the Egyptians by the "arm of God." This present prophecy indicates that this very same "arm of God"—who appeared as a Savior to the ancient people—would be revealed to all the nations, as if he had previously been hidden. Moreover, as for the **salvation** which he says all the ends of the earth shall see, he made it even clearer by saying: "I will make your salvation heard." You should know that in the Hebrew tongue, this "salvation" is addressed by the name of **Jesus**. <note>The Hebrew name Yeshua (Jesus) literally means "salvation" or "Yahweh is salvation." In another sense, one could say that "fire" and "chariots" were brought down alongside His presence because of the siege that overtook Jerusalem after His arrival among us. Not long after His coming, His Temple was set on fire and suffered ultimate desolation, and the city was surrounded by armies and hostile camps. After these events, the gathering of all the nations reached its fulfillment, exactly as foretold in the prophecy. 

Who would not be amazed to hear the Lord saying through the prophet, "I am coming to gather all nations and tongues," when they see the assemblies of the nations being brought together in the name of Christ throughout the whole earth, through the presence and calling of our Savior Jesus Christ? Who would not marvel at the tongues of all nations calling upon the one God and Lord in all sorts of dialects? # PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, BOOK VII

...his visitation was foretold, and where on earth it was heralded that he would be born, and from what lineage it was proclaimed he would come forth.

->What is the place of the Lord’s visitation among men? From Isaiah.<-

The prediction of the disbelief of the Jewish nation toward Christ, and a sign given to them by the Lord. Through this, every race of people comes to know God. Following this knowledge, the total destruction of the Jewish nation was to follow, and foreigners and enemies would occupy their land, while the land which was previously a desert <note>Referring to the Gentile world</note> would become fertile through the cultivation of the Gospel. The Church gathered from the nations is revealed in this manner, just as the wonderful Evangelist John, with a voice greater than a human’s, speaks of the divinity <note>original: "theologōn"</note> of our Savior and Lord, namely the Word of God himself. Beginning at the very start of the Sacred Scripture, John presents both his divinity and his bodily visitation among men: *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning with God. All things were made through Him.* Next, he adds: *And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us.* 

In the same way, the divinely inspired prophet <note>Isaiah</note>, speaking through the Spirit of God, sees in advance his glorious manifestation. He describes this divine discourse <note>original: "theologian"</note> in this way: *I saw the Lord of Hosts <note>original: "Sabaoth"</note> sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, and the house was full of his glory, and Seraphim stood around him. Each one had six wings; with two they covered their face, with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew. And one cried to another and said: Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.* 

The prophet then adds: *And I heard the voice of the Lord saying: Whom shall I send, and who will go to this people? And I said: Here am I, send me. And he said to me: Go, and say to this people: You shall hear indeed, but not understand; and you shall see indeed, but not perceive. For the heart of this people has become calloused, and their ears are heavy of hearing, and their eyes they have closed, lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn back, and I should heal them. And I said: How long, Lord? And he said: Until the cities are laid waste, so as not to be inhabited, and the houses so as not to have men.*

Is it not right to say that the prophet saw the same Lord who appeared to and spoke with our forefather Abraham, as we demonstrated in the preceding books? For we have already learned that he is both God and Lord, while also being the Angel and the Commander-in-Chief of the Lord’s host. This present passage, foretelling his entrance into the world of men, envisions his dwelling in a royal palace, regarding which the prophet says he saw him *sitting on a throne, high and lifted up.* This is that very throne of his revealed in the 131st Psalm <note>Psalm 132 in modern Bibles</note>, and in another where it says: *Thy throne, O God, is forever and ever.* Upon this throne, the God and Father of all, the Creator, commanded his Only-begotten and Beloved Son to sit, saying: *Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.* John the Evangelist confirms this interpretation for us, who, after the aforementioned...

# EUSEBIUS

...the voices of Isaiah in which it was said, *For this people’s heart has grown fat, and they have heard heavily with their ears, and I have closed their eyes*, it adds as if speaking of Christ, saying, *These things Isaiah said when he saw his glory and spoke of him.* <note>Eusebius is quoting John 12:40-41, where the Evangelist identifies the "Lord" in Isaiah's vision as Christ.</note> Thus, the prophet, seeing the Son of God upon the Father’s throne, honored with the establishment of glory and kingship, and being visited by the Holy Spirit, describes in the words that follow his progress toward men and his birth from before all ages. He bears witness beforehand to the knowledge and glorification that would spread throughout the whole earth, introducing the Seraphim <note>A class of celestial beings described in Isaiah’s vision.</note> surrounding him and saying: *Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts <note>original: "Sabaoth"</note>, the whole earth is full of his glory.*

And who might these Seraphim be that act as a bodyguard for the Christ of God? Perhaps they are choirs of angels and divine powers, or even the prophets and apostles. The name "Seraphim" might be interpreted as "the beginning of their mouth" <note>original: "archē stomatos autōn." This is a specific etymological interpretation Eusebius uses to link the Seraphim to the "mouths" of the apostles.</note> Such are the prophets and apostles, through whose mouths the first fruits <note>term: "first fruits" (aparchē) - the initial part of a harvest, here meaning the beginning of the Gospel message.</note> of the saving preaching were produced. By attaining this title, those whose powers are named "wings" through the Holy Spirit hide the first and the last things of the knowledge of the Word of God—as these are ineffable and incomprehensible by nature—but they reveal the middle things of his economy <note>term: "economy" (oikonomia) - the divine plan for human salvation, specifically the life and work of Jesus on earth.</note> toward him. For these things alone are known to human nature, while the things beyond and the things after these are kept silent in secret. 

There may also be divine and heavenly powers through which the Seraphim are interpreted. For this reason it is said: *He who makes his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.* <note>Psalm 104:4</note> These cry out and shout to one another according to their own power, presenting the holiness of the one who is being discussed as God. Above all, they glorify God, speaking of his divinity because not only heaven and all things in heaven happen to be full of his glory, but all the earth also participates in the same power. This is because of his future presence among men from the heavens, as the word prophesies in order. It heralds his birth from a Virgin and his glorification which is spread through this birth to all the earth.

Now, "Lord of Hosts" <note>original: "Sabaoth"</note> is translated as "Lord of the powers." He himself would be the "Chief Captain of the Lord's power," whom the divine powers call "Lord of Hosts" again in the 23rd Psalm <note>Psalm 24 in modern Bibles.</note> when they prepare his ascent from earth to heaven. Through these powers they say: *Lift up your gates, O you rulers, and be lifted up, you everlasting doors, and the King of Glory shall enter.* Who is this King of Glory? *The Lord of the powers, he is the King of Glory.* <note>Psalm 24:10</note> The Hebrew term for "Christ," his servant, calls him "Lord of Hosts." 

And since he is the King of Glory, and because through his visitation all the earth was to be filled with his glory, it is reasonably found not only in the prophet but also in the Psalm which the prophet possesses. In the vision it says, *the whole earth is full of his glory*, and in the Psalm, the beginning declares: *The earth is the Lord’s and the fullness thereof, the world and all who dwell in it.* After these things are accomplished, the prophet continues by bearing witness that even if the whole earth is filled with his glory, the Jewish nation will not accept him. For this reason he says: *And the Lord said*—namely the Lord of Hosts who was seen—*Whom shall I send? And who will go to this people?* And I said: *Behold, here am I, send me.* And he said: *Go, and say*

# THE PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, BOOK 6
193
Rr.i.

> » Go to this people and say: "You shall indeed hear, but you shall not understand; and you shall indeed see, but you shall not perceive." For the heart of this people has grown fat, and they have heard heavily with their ears, and they have closed their eyes, lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn back, and I should heal them.

Through these words, the prophet directly foretells the coming opposition of the Jewish people toward Him <note>Referring to Christ.</note>. He predicts that they would see Him, yet would not acknowledge who He was. Even as He spoke among them and taught them, they would hear but not understand at all what He discussed with them, nor would they grasp the lessons of the new teaching He handed down. The Evangelist John serves as a witness to the fulfillment of these words regarding our Savior, saying:

> » Though He had performed so many signs before them, they did not believe in Him, so that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spoke: "Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?" For this reason they could not believe, because Isaiah said again: "He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, so that they should not see with their eyes, and perceive with their heart, and turn back, and I should heal them."

Isaiah said these things when he saw His glory and spoke of Him. <note>John 12:37-41.</note> Without question, then, the Evangelist refers the things seen in Isaiah’s divine visions to Christ. It is the Jewish people, therefore, who did not accept the Lord seen by the prophets, as was foretold of them. The divine oracle tells the prophet—who had seen the Lord of Hosts <note>original: "Sabaoth"</note>—to say to the Jewish nation that they too would one day see the same Lord, but would not understand who He was; and though they would hear Him speaking and teaching them, they would not comprehend because their hearts had become hardened. 

Isaiah, having prophesied these things in the words we have set forth, then describes in his historical narrative an assault of enemies against Ahaz <note>King of Judah (c. 732–716 BCE) during the Syro-Ephraimite War.</note>, as the affairs of the Jewish kingdom were then reaching a crisis. He signifies that the destruction of these physical enemies would happen immediately and not in the distant future. However, these physical enemies were symbols of intellectual and invisible enemies—certain demons and hidden powers. We discussed these at the beginning of this entire work: how not only the Jewish nation but the whole human race had fallen for a long time into every form of wickedness, specifically into godless idolatry. The prophet reveals that these powers would not be defeated in any other way than through the foretold arrival <note>term: "epidemia" (arrival/advent) - used by early Christians to describe the presence of God on earth in the person of Jesus.</note> of the Divine Word among men, who would take up a human frame <note>original: "skenos" (tabernacle or tent), a common metaphor for the human body.</note> from a virgin who had never known marriage. It is now time to discuss why this was necessary for Him.

---

### Concerning the Advent of our Savior.

Since "through man death entered into the world," as the Apostle says <note>Referring to Paul in Romans 5:12 or 1 Corinthians 15:21.</note>, it was surely necessary that through a man the victory over death should also be awarded. Thus, the "body of death" would be revealed as a "body of life," and the kingdom of sin, which previously operated within the mortal body, would be destroyed, with sin no longer ruling it but righteousness instead. And since, through the sins of the flesh, the fall of all humanity had occurred long ago, it was fitting that through one who was sinless and free from all unmixed evil, the trophies of victory against the Enemy should be raised. And who were these enemies but those who of old, through the pleasures of the flesh, had wrestled the human race to the ground? And clearly...

# OF EUSEBIUS
### [THE PROOF OF THE GOSPEL]

194

It was necessary for the Word of God <note>Greek: *Logos*. In Christian theology, the pre-existent second person of the Trinity.</note>, when He was about to converse with men and deliver the lessons of piety to the ears of the flesh, and to present wonders and miraculous works to the eyes of men, and to manifest the clear power of God, to do these things through an instrument <note>Greek: *organon*. Eusebius frequently describes the human body of Christ as a tool or "instrument" used by the divine Word.</note> familiar to us. For it was not possible for the eyes of men to see anything more than what is physical, nor for the ear to hear anything more than a sound carried by a tongue. 

Therefore, so that through the senses of the body we might grasp the concept of things intellectual and incorporeal, the Word of God Himself assumed the instrument related and known to us; and through it, He set all His saving works before those who were the eyewitnesses and firsthand hearers of His divine words and deeds. He did these things while being in no way bound by the necessities of the body as we are, nor diminishing His own nature, nor bowing down from the greatness of His own divinity. Though He was present in a body as the Word—who is everywhere, fills all things, and pervades all things—He was not like a human soul <note>Eusebius is distinguishing Christ from ordinary humans; while a human soul is "trapped" or limited by the body, the Divine Word remains infinite even while incarnate.</note>. Nor did He bring upon Himself any filth, corruption, or defilement from the flesh He had assumed, because He is incorporeal by nature, immaterial, and without flesh. As the Word of God, in His own power and by means beyond our description, He carried out the entire Economy <term>Economy: (Greek: *oikonomia*) The divine plan or "management" of the world, specifically referring here to the Incarnation and God’s interaction with humanity.</term>, sharing His own attributes but not suffering in return from the things foreign to Him. 

Therefore, one should not fear the incarnate Economy, since the Unpolluted One was not defiled, nor was the Undefiled One stained by the flesh, nor was the impassible <note>Incapable of suffering or being changed by external forces.</note> Word of God corrupted by the specific nature of the body; for not even the rays of the sun would suffer anything by touching dead bodies or bodies of all kinds. Rather, by the divine Word, that which was perishable was transformed, and was rendered holy and immortal, since this was His will. Indeed, He served the intentions, counsels, and actions of the Spirit. This entire matter, concerning the most man-loving God and the Word of God, was proclaimed for the healing and salvation of all men by the voices of the prophets, who from ancient times foretold His wondrous birth from a virgin. 

The prophet <note>Isaiah.</note> very necessarily places the birth of Christ from a virgin at the forefront as something to be heeded, calling out a saving word to those who listen: "Unless you believe, you shall not understand." Following this, he brings in the things that happen in this manner:

<margin>„</margin> "Unless you believe, you shall not understand." And the Lord spoke again 
<margin>„</margin> to Ahaz, saying, "Ask a sign for yourself from the Lord your God, in the 
<margin>„</margin> depth or in the height." And Ahaz said, "I will not ask, nor will I test the 
<margin>„</margin> Lord." And he <note>Isaiah.</note> said, "Hear then, O house of David! Is it a small 
<margin>„</margin> thing for you to provide a struggle for men, and how do you provide 
<margin>„</margin> a struggle for the Lord? Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign. 
<margin>„</margin> Behold, the virgin shall conceive in her womb and bear a son, and you 
<margin>„</margin> shall call His name Immanuel. He shall eat butter and honey before He 
<margin>„</margin> knows how to prefer evil or chooses the good; because before the child 
<margin>„</margin> knows good or evil, He refuses wickedness to choose the good. And the 
<margin>„</margin> land which you fear shall be abandoned because of the presence of the 
<margin>„</margin> two kings." <note>Isaiah 7:9–16. This is the central prophecy cited by early Christians to prove the Virgin Birth.</note>

Such was the nature of the prophecy. It is worth noting how the account begins with a testimony to the readers, stating that if they do not believe, they will not understand. And he signaled this by necessity, showing that there is a need not only for understanding, but also for faith in those who read. And not only faith, but also understanding. Hence, those of the circumcision <note>A common early Christian term for the Jewish people.</note> who did not believe in the Christ of God, even now when they hear these things, have not yet understood them to this day...
