...was prophesied, so that the prediction might be clearly proven true in their case. For though they hear the prophecies concerning Christ all day long with their ears, they do not hear them with their understanding. The cause of their ignorance is nothing other than unbelief, and this is confirmed by the prophecy which speaks truly about them and to them. For it says:

> "If you do not believe, neither shall you understand." <note>A quote from the Septuagint version of Isaiah 7:9. Modern translations often render this as "If you do not stand firm in your faith, you will not stand at all."</note>

But what if the Scripture did not use the word "virgin" <note>Greek: *parthenos*</note> but called her a "young woman" <note>Greek: *neanis*</note>? For the Jews claim this is the wording found in their versions. We must ask: what kind of "sign" worthy of God’s promise would it be if a young woman were to conceive in the usual way, as all women do, through intercourse with a man? How would the one born from her be God? And not just God, but "God with us"? This is what "Emmanuel" signifies, the name the prophet says must be given to the one being born. For it says:

> "Behold, the virgin shall conceive in her womb, and shall bear a son, and you shall call his name Emmanuel; which, being interpreted, is: God with us." <note>Isaiah 7:14, as quoted in Matthew 1:23.</note>

What "struggle" would God have, or what "labor" and "toil" would be involved in the ordinary birth of a woman? In our copies <note>The Septuagint (LXX), the Greek translation of the Old Testament used by the early Church.</note>, translated long ago from the Hebrew by seventy men—translators proven for their accuracy in their ancestral learning—it is recorded as follows:

> "Is it a small thing for you to provide a struggle for men? And how do you provide a struggle for the Lord? Therefore, the Lord Himself will give you a sign. Behold, the virgin shall conceive in her womb, and shall bear a son, who shall be called God-with-us."

As I said, this is what the name Emmanuel is intended to reveal. However, in the copies used by the Jews themselves, according to the translation of Aquila <note>Aquila of Sinope was a 2nd-century proselyte to Judaism who produced an extremely literal Greek translation to rival the Septuagint.</note>—and though Aquila was not a Jew by birth, the text is stated this way even by him:

> "He said: Hear now, house of David; is it a small thing for you to weary men, that you weary also my Lord God? Therefore He Himself will give you a sign. Behold, the young woman <note>Greek: *neanis*</note> conceives in her womb, and bears a son, and you shall call his name Emmanuel."

In the version of Symmachus <note>Symmachus the Ebionite, a late 2nd-century translator.</note>, it stands similarly. Symmachus is said to have been an Ebionite—the Ebionites are a sect of those called "Jews" who are said to believe in Christ. In his version, it also reads:

> "Hear, house of David, is it not enough for you to weary men, that you weary my God? Therefore He Himself will give you a sign. Behold, the young woman conceives and bears a son, and you shall call his name Emmanuel."

Because the Jewish nation, by their hardness of character and stubbornness toward piety, caused sweat, labor, and no small toil and struggle for the God-loving prophets of old, the text says: "Is it not enough for you to weary the prophets of God, and to provide a struggle for men? But now you even weary my God, and provide a struggle even for my God?" For this is how Theodotion <note>Another 2nd-century translator of the Hebrew Bible into Greek.</note> also rendered it. The prophet specifically calls Him "his own God," and not the God of those to whom he is speaking. He describes God as being "wearied" and "stripping for the struggle" <note>Eusebius uses a metaphor of an athlete preparing for a contest to describe the difficulty God faces in dealing with the people's unbelief.</note>. He would not have said "my God" regarding the God who is over all the Jews, for they had preserved the worship of the God who is the Creator of all things from their fathers. What then would be this "struggle" and "labor," or the "toil" of the God being prophesied, other than His coming into human nature? According to our tradition and the translation of the Seventy, He is born of a virgin; but according to the version currently circulating among the Jews, He is born of a young woman. Yet you will see even in Moses that a woman who is admittedly a virgin is called a "young woman." Or...

Ahaz <note>King of Judah (c. 732–716 BC) who was threatened by the alliance of Syria and northern Israel.</note> loathed or abhorred their land, growing weary and troubled by it. And this is: the Virgin bearing "God with us" <note>original: "Emmanuel"</note>. 

And indeed, it is clear to those who examine histories that until the times of the appearance of our Savior Jesus Christ, the succession of kings from ancestral lines still stood even in Damascus. Certainly, the holy Apostle mentions Aretas, the king of the Damascenes <note>Referring to 2 Corinthians 11:32, where Paul escapes from Damascus under King Aretas IV.</note>. And for the nation of the Jews, the order and the kingdom—though no longer according to the Law <note>A reference to the fact that the Herodian kings were of Idumean descent, not of the Davidic line.</note>—had not yet failed then. For Herod and those after him, who lived at the time of our Savior, did not carry the succession of rule from the line of David. 

But after His appearance, and the evangelical preaching to all men concerning the child born of the Virgin, the land was immediately dissolved from the face of the two kings. For from that time, when the Roman monarchy prevailed over the nations, all local rule by ethnic leaders <term>ethnarchia</term> and multiple rulers <term>polyarchia</term> was dissolved. And after not much time, the matters of the prophecy reached their end—specifically stated in this way.

But according to its deeper meaning <note>original: "dianoian" – the spiritual or intellectual sense as opposed to the literal "lexin".</note>, the prophetic word signifies the passionless, calm, and peaceful state of every soul; it signifies that such a soul alone receives the God who was born, namely Emmanuel. For while the one Christ and the Word announced by Him reigns in the human soul, the former enemies have fled—two kinds of impiety: the one that subjected men to idolatry and false belief <note>original: "heterodoxia"</note> among many-godded doctrines, and the one that works perversely in morals. Of these, the physical kings mentioned of old were symbols. One of them, the Damascene, is a certain image of the error of the nations regarding idols; the other, of those who revolted from Jerusalem—that is, those who fell away from the worship according to the Law of God.

That it is fitting to receive these things figuratively <note>original: "tropikos"</note>, one might learn also from the things following, through which the Word prophesies that in the day of Emmanuel certain "flies" and "bees" will come upon the nations of the Jews—some from Egypt, some from the Assyrians—and will shave the head, the feet, and the beard. And that a man will nourish a heifer of the herd and two sheep, and other strange things will occur at the same time, which are by no means understood according to the literal word, but are contemplated only according to the inner meaning. These things, then, are so. As for how the present scripture...

The prophecy foretold that such things would happen in the day of Emmanuel. He says the Lord calls for "flies" in that day "which rule over part of the river of Egypt, and the fly which is in the land of the Assyrians." These "flies," I believe, refer to the more wicked souls of idolatrous men, or perhaps unclean powers and men who are named "flies" because they delight in Egyptian sacrifices and the blood of idols. The other "fly" <note>The Septuagint Greek text Eusebius uses here describes the Assyrian power as a stinging insect, likely a bee, though the word "fly" is repeated.</note> is a creature that carries a sting, knowing how to rule, how to make war, and how to defend itself and wound those who cause it grief.

For when the Assyrians pour in, the land will be made desolate; it is as if the Lord and God of all has commanded a gathering to take control of the whole of Judea because of their unbelief in Christ "in the day of Emmanuel," he says. By these figures, he signifies that foreign and warlike nations would inhabit Jerusalem and the Judean land. And just as our Savior...

<margin>„</margin>He prophesied in other words, saying, *And Jerusalem shall be trampled by the nations.* <note>original: "καὶ ἰερουσαλὴμ ἔσται πατουμένη ὑπὸ ἐθνῶν" — a reference to the words of Jesus in Luke 21:24.</note> This prophecy reached its fulfillment not long after the voice of our Savior, when the Romans took the city and settled foreigners there, who remain in that place to this day. In these words, he is hinting at the Romans. For I believe that by the name of the "Assyrians," the prophecy signifies whichever kingdom of the nations is dominant at any particular time. <margin>„</margin>Roman rule. Regarding the "King of the Assyrians," <note>Eusebius is comparing different Greek versions of the Old Testament to clarify the grammar.</note> Aquila translates it as "in the kingdom 
<margin>„</margin>of the Assyrians," while Theodotion renders it "in the King of the Assyrians," and Symmachus does the same. They make it clear that the Word does not threaten to shave the head of the King of Assyria himself, but rather that the things prophesied regarding the Jewish nation will be carried out **by means of** that razor—that is, by the King of the Assyrians. The outcome of events bears witness to this interpretation. If one looks closely, many other things said in the prophecies as if addressed to the person of the "Assyrians" cannot possibly fit the historical Assyrians, but instead apply to the universal kingdom of the nations that dominates from time to time. For example, we find that the Persians are also called "Assyrians" by the Hebrews. For this reason, we have understood the Word to be hinting at the Roman Empire. We see that nation being humbled and brought low by God after the appearance of our Savior. Let no one suppose, however, that I am saying all things mentioned in the Divine Scriptures concerning the Assyrians must refer to the Romans. That would be a great error. Rather, there are certain prophetic voices intertwined with the testimonies concerning Christ which we claim hint at the Romans through the name of the Assyrians. This is because the interpretation of the name always signifies the kingdom of the nations that prevails at a given time, as we shall demonstrate when the proper time comes. And as I search out the reason for this interpretation within myself, I believe the prophetic oracles did not mention the Romans by name for no other reason than this: the teaching of our Savior Jesus Christ was destined to shine forth to all people during the Roman Empire, and the prophetic scriptures were to be published in the city of Rome itself and among all the nations under Roman rule. Therefore, so that no offense or displeasure might be caused to the rulers of the time by an explicit written condemnation of them, the Word concealed the matter through riddles. This is done in many other places, and notably in the visions of Daniel, just as in the present prophecy, where he gives the name "Assyrians" to those who would humble them. <meta>This page continues Eusebius’s interpretation of Isaiah 7. He moves from the "razor" (symbolizing the Roman conquest) to the specific fate of the land and the people following the coming of Emmanuel (Christ).</meta>

# EUSEBIUS

He prophesies that the entire world <note>original: "σύμπαντα κόσμον" — here referring to the established religious and social order</note> for the Jewish nation will vanish after the arrival of Emmanuel. Furthermore, on that designated day—clearly the day of Emmanuel—at the appearance of Christ, he says:

» *A man shall nourish a young cow and*
» *two sheep. And it shall come to pass, from the abundance of milk produced, he shall eat butter and honey;*
» *everyone who is left upon the land shall eat them.* <note>Isaiah 7:21–22</note>

Through these words, one might say he is hinting at a famine and a state of scarcity for the "people of the circumcision" <note>The Jewish people</note>. They will no longer be nourished by the grain of their natural food, nor will they plow the earth, sow, or reap. They will possess neither flocks of sheep nor herds of cattle, but will be reduced to keeping only two sheep and a single young cow, living off their milk.

Alternatively, looking at it another way, one might say "the survivor left upon the land" hints at the choir of Apostles and Evangelists from the circumcision who believed in our Lord and Savior. Each of them, having become a "remnant according to the election of grace" <note>A reference to Romans 11:5</note> and therefore a "survivor" in the world, is said to nourish a young cow and two sheep. These represent the orders within each **Church**: one order being those who lead, and two being those who are subordinate. 

Of the people in the Church of Christ, the two subordinate orders are divided into the **faithful** and those not yet deemed worthy of the <term>laver of rebirth</term> <note>original: "λουτροῦ παλιγγενεσίας" — a technical term for Baptism</note>. To these latter ones, the divine Apostle says: *I gave you milk to drink, not solid food.* <note>1 Corinthians 3:2</note> Those who have already become more mature he reasonably calls a "young cow," as they are the offspring of more perfect "oxen"—just as the Apostle himself was. Speaking of himself and those who labored alongside him, he says: *Is it for oxen that God is concerned? Or does He say it altogether for our sakes?* <note>1 Corinthians 9:9–10</note>

The great order of those presiding over the Church, who are entrusted with nourishing and "farming" the souls of men, might be the ones named the "young cow." They are the offspring of the Apostolic teachings and traditions. These leaders are said to increase in virtue to such an extent that, from their great fruitfulness, they provide so much "rational milk" <note>original: "λογικὸν... γάλα" — intellectual or spiritual nourishment</note> through their introductory teachings that thousands of others are nourished by them.

While these things are revealed concerning those who are "left upon the land," the prophecy foretells that something else will happen on that day—that is, in the time of the presence of Emmanuel. What is this? He says:

» *Every place where there were a thousand vines*
» *worth a thousand silver shekels shall become a wasteland and thorns.*
» *Men shall enter there with bows and arrows* <note>Isaiah 7:23–24</note>

—clearly referring to the enemies—

» *because the whole land shall be a wasteland and thorns.*

Observe how the Word prophesies what will happen to the Jewish nation in the "Day of Emmanuel." I mean the time of the rising of the **Rational Light** <note>original: "λογικοῦ φωτός" — the Light of Christ/Reason</note> which has shone upon all men through our Savior. He foretells that unclean and warring powers—those that formerly operated among the nations, whether Assyrian or by the hand of the "Assyrians" <note>Eusebius identifies the "Assyrians" of prophecy with the Roman armies</note>—whom the Lord brings in like a flooding river, will come upon their country because they have become worthy of such things. 

He says these powers will "rest" in the valleys, in the clefts of the rocks, in caves, and in every cranny. In a spiritual sense, this means they will rest in their souls, in the senses of their bodies, in their reasonings, and in their fractured minds. But in the literal sense, it means throughout their entire country. Who would not be struck with wonder, seeing with his own eyes that the land of the Jews is now a place full of their enemies?

<summary>Eusebius interprets Isaiah 7, arguing that "milk and honey" represents either the literal poverty of the Jews after the Roman conquest or the spiritual nourishment provided by the Apostles to the early Church. He concludes by describing the desolation of Judea as a fulfillment of prophecy due to the rejection of Christ.</summary>

### GOSPEL PROOF BOOK 7

->PAGE 201<-

...of **Judea**, and the foreigners and idolaters who have settled and found rest in all their cities and lands. The Word says that the "razor" will not only deal with them in this way, but by this razor—which we understand to be the **King of the Assyrians** <note>Eusebius identifies the 'Assyrian' here with the Roman power that eventually conquered Jerusalem</note>—He will shave their head, the hair of their feet, and their beard. This plainly means He will shave away all the glory that formerly surrounded them.

On that same day and at that same time, it was fitting that they should be reduced from God's wealth to extreme poverty. They would lack "living rational beings" and solid spiritual food, contenting themselves with being nourished by milk like infants through introductory teaching. Furthermore, their vineyards will become a wilderness. For as the same prophet says:

<margin>''</margin> The farmer and master waited for the vineyard to produce grapes, 
<margin>''</margin> but it produced thorns—not righteousness, but a cry of distress. <note>A reference to Isaiah 5:7, playing on the Hebrew wordplay between 'mishpat' (justice) and 'mispach' (bloodshed/outcry)</note>

<margin>''</margin> Therefore, having removed its hedge and torn down its wall, He testifies that He will turn the 
<margin>''</margin> vineyard into a wilderness and deliver it to enemies. He says they will enter there 
<margin>''</margin> with arrows and bows, having received authority from God. 
<margin>''</margin> God delivered it to them not without judgment, but most justly, because all 
<margin>''</margin> their land had become a wilderness and thorns. 

Because they turned themselves into a wilderness and thorns, He says that those who received authority over them will enter there with arrows and bows.

Do not wonder if these things are delivered obscurely and through riddles. The reason for this "divine economy of the word" <note>original: "οἰκονομίας τοῦ λόγου" — the strategic way God communicates in Scripture</note> has already been stated: it was intended to hide the ultimate destruction of the Jewish nation so that the Scripture might be preserved by them for the improvement and benefit of us Gentiles. For if it had been openly confessed to them, and the prophecies had proclaimed good things for the Gentiles, no one of the **circumcision** <note>The Jewish people</note> would have cared for these records. Rather, viewing the prophecies as hostile and opposed to themselves, they would have destroyed them. Then it would no longer be possible for us from the Gentiles to use the prophets' testimonies concerning our own salvation.

But since so much is to happen to the Jewish nation on the "Day of Emmanuel," let us interpret the other side of the prophecy without despair. It speaks of "the survivor left among them," about whom the Apostle says:

<margin>''</margin> *A remnant has come to be according to the election of grace.* <note>Romans 11:5</note>

This survivor will nourish a young cow and two sheep, and from the abundance of milk produced, he will eat butter and honey. In our second interpretation, this "survivor" represents the entire apostolic choir of the disciples of our Savior, **Jesus Christ**. 

Just as this survivor is prophesied to thrive, while the whole land of the Jewish nation—their "vineyard"—is turned into a wilderness and delivered to enemies, so too, on the other hand, it is prophesied that "every mountain that used to be plowed shall be plowed." I believe the **Church** of our Savior Jesus Christ is hinted at in this way, of which He Himself says:

<margin>''</margin> *A city set on a hill cannot be hidden.* <note>Matthew 5:14</note>

For I believe the delightful, lofty, and high-soaring nature of the Church's way of life <note>original: "πολιτεύματος" — referring to the spiritual citizenship or conduct of Christians</note> is allegorized through these things as a "mountain." This mountain, it says, "shall be plowed," so that no fear shall come there. It shall be changed so much from its former desolation, wilderness, and thorns, as to become fit...

<summary>Eusebius explains that Isaiah's prophecy of the "razor" refers to the Roman conquest of Judea. He argues that the destruction was described in riddles so the Jews would preserve the texts for the eventual benefit of the Gentiles and the Church.</summary>
<keywords>Eusebius, Demonstratio Evangelica, Isaiah 7, Romans, destruction of Jerusalem, the Remnant, the Church as a Mountain, allegory, Gentiles, Jewish nation</keywords>

...into a place for sheep to graze and for oxen to tread. You may also consider how the Church of Christ—which was formerly a dry wasteland and full of thorns—has, through His grace, undergone such a great change. The "grass" of **rational fruitfulness** <note>original: "λογικῆς καρποφορίας" — Eusebius uses "rational" or "logical" to describe spiritual, rather than physical, growth</note> has flourished so much that even those who are apostolic and simple are able to enjoy it. Those who have advanced from more basic nourishment and "farming" have left behind the pit. This reminds us of how the divine Apostle taught us—as we noted in the pages before this—when he asked: 

» *Is it for oxen that God is concerned? Or does He speak entirely for our sake? It was indeed written for our sake, because the plowman ought to plow in hope, and the thresher should thresh in hope of sharing the crop.* <note>Eusebius is quoting 1 Corinthians 9:9–10 to explain that the "oxen" mentioned in the prophecy are actually the Apostles and teachers of the Church</note> 

Thus, the former desert and wasteland was transformed at the coming of Christ, so that it became suitable for the "rational oxen" <note>the Apostles</note> to perform their proper spiritual farming. Consider then the place where honey is found, and how a mindset flows from His springs. The Word says that the land which was not long ago fruitful—that which was once worth a **thousand shekels**—shall become a wasteland and full of thorns. The whole land shall become thorns for them, because you will not walk among the thorns and wasteland; rather, one will enter there with arrows and bows. 

Every mountain shall suffer this. From being a former wasteland of thorns and briers, it is changed into a place for sheep to graze and for oxen to tread, so that what was once plowed shall be plowed again, and there shall be no fear there. By these things, I believe the extraordinary knowledge of our Savior is clearly signaled, as well as the events that happened simultaneously to the godless Jews <note>original: "ἀθέοις ἰουδαίοις" — a common polemical term in this era for those who did not accept Christ</note> and the rest of the nations. 

This marks a reversal for both groups: for the one, a change from better to worse; for the Church gathered from the nations, an end to its former desolation and a move toward **fruitfulness according to God**. These things were prophesied to be fulfilled at one and the same time—the appearance of **Emmanuel**. It is shown that these predictions reached their fulfillment at no other time than after the coming of our Savior. This is evident through the visible destruction of the Jews and through the Church established among the nations. 

For if, at the time of our Savior's coming—Jesus Christ Himself—the monarchical rule of the Jews had not ceased, and if we did not see before our eyes that the land is now "farmed" by foreign nations and idolaters who live there; if all that was once most venerable has not turned into a wasteland and thorns at the very hour of their sacred glory; and if "unclean" idolaters and their enemies had not come with arrows and bows, stirred up from foreign lands to rest in their territories and take possession of every place and city—then the prophecy would be unfulfilled. 

And conversely, if the nations that believe in Him had not changed from being a wasteland of thorns and a lack of spiritual farming, and through the teaching of our Savior received a rational fruitfulness toward God; and if, in addition to this, those who saw Christ with their eyes had not disbelieved, and those who heard Him teaching had not refused to listen; and if the rest of the prophecy had not clearly met its end starting from the times of Jesus our Savior—then He would not be the One prophesied. But if the results of these words are clear even to a "blind man," as the saying goes, and were fulfilled at no other time than starting from His appearance, then what more is there to say?

He uses Paul's words from 1 Corinthians to argue that the "oxen" in the prophecy represent the Apostles cultivating a new spiritual harvest.</summary>

# PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, Book 7

...even if someone is doubtful regarding his knowledge, why does he not, with a fair-minded logic, find proof for the origin of His deeds from things that are still visible today? And what might these visible things be, other than the unbelief of the Jews toward Him? This is clearly being fulfilled according to the oracle which says: **» By hearing you shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing you shall see, and shall not perceive. For the heart of this people has grown fat.** <note>Quoting Isaiah 6:9–10, a passage frequently used by early Christians to explain why the Jewish leadership rejected Jesus.</note> Or consider the siege of Jerusalem and the total desolation of their ancient sanctuary, and the settlement of foreign nations in their land, who पुन्हा once more keep them in subjection with "stings"—that is, with harsh imperial commands. This is what the examples of the **flies and the bees** <note>In the previous section, Eusebius interpreted the "flies of Egypt" and "bees of Assyria" as symbols for the Roman armies and their oppressive taxation/laws.</note> intended to show. Above all, there is the transformation of the Gentiles from their former spiritual desert into the **knowledge of God**. Who, seeing these things with their own eyes, would not be struck with wonder? Who would not confess that the prophecies are truly divine, hearing them lying in books for a whole thousand years, knowing that these and ten thousand other things were never brought to fulfillment until after His saving arrival?

If, therefore, the prophecy is marvelous, and the fulfillment of the prophecies is even more marvelous in every respect, why should one disbelieve if the "prophetess" <note>Eusebius identifies the "prophetess" in Isaiah 8 with the Virgin Mary from Isaiah 7.</note> and the progress of the one prophesied also received a paradoxical origin of birth, beyond all human nature? For the clear sight of the remaining miracles, being no less significant, compels us by its own knowledge to accept the testimony of all the deeds performed by Him.

But following these things, after the mention of the land becoming a place for the grazing and treading of oxen, a second prophecy is joined, which completes the one already set forth, beginning with: **» And the Lord said to me, "Take for yourself a large scroll."** Let us examine this one as well from our abundance of evidence.

->From the same author.<-

Concerning a **new writing**—evidently the **New Testament** <note>term: New Testament (original: "καινῆς διαθήκης"). Eusebius explicitly links the "new scroll" of Isaiah to the Christian New Testament.</note>—it is said that a **prophetess** shall conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear a son. This son, having conquered his enemies and foes, shall be met with unbelief by the Jews, but shall be a savior to the Gentiles. The suffering that the Jewish nation shall endure after their unbelief toward Him is revealed in the same passage.

» **And the Lord said to me, "Take for yourself a new, large scroll, and write in it with a man’s pen: 'Make a swift booty of spoils.' For it is at hand. And get for me faithful men as witnesses: Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Barachiah." And I went to the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. And the Lord said to me, "Call his name: 'Spoil quickly, plunder swiftly.' For before the child knows how to call for his father or mother, he shall take the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria before the king of the Assyrians."** <note>Isaiah 8:1–4. The name "Maher-shalal-hash-baz" is translated here into English commands as Eusebius would have understood them from the Greek Septuagint.</note>

This present prophecy follows the one previously set. For she who was said to be a virgin and to bear "God-with-us" <note>Emmanuel</note> is, in the present context, named a **prophetess**. To the question of how she shall conceive while being unmarried, the Word now teaches us by saying, **"I went to the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son."** These things must be understood as being done by the **Holy Spirit**, by whom the prophet was inspired when he spoke. For the Spirit itself...

# EUSEBIUS

...confesses that the Holy Spirit was with the prophetess. This was clearly fulfilled at the birth of our Savior Jesus Christ, when the angel Gabriel was sent by God to a city in Galilee named Nazareth, to a virgin betrothed to a man named Joseph, of the house and family of David. To her he said:
>> "Greetings, favored one, the Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women."
And again: 
>> "Do not fear, for you have found favor with God. And behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus."
When Mary said, "How will this be, since I do not know a man?" he answered:
>> "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore, the holy child to be born will be called the Son of God."

In the former prophecy regarding the birth of Emmanuel, it was said that before the child knows good or evil, the land would be abandoned by the two kings who were besieging it: one being the king of Samaria, and the other the king of Damascus. But in the present prophecy, before the child knows how to call "Father" or "Mother," he will take the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria. He prophesied that these kings would be destroyed even earlier, at the birth of Emmanuel. 

Now, in a literal sense <note>original: αἰσθητῶς, meaning "perceptibly" or historically</note>, in the days of Ahaz, king of Judah, during the time of Isaiah the prophet himself, two kings—forming an alliance against the successors of David—were conducting a siege, as has been shown previously. One was the king of the idolatrous nations at Damascus; the other was the king of the Jewish multitude in the city called Samaria in Palestine, which those in our time call **Sebaste** <note>Herod the Great renamed Samaria "Sebaste" in honor of Emperor Augustus (Sebastos in Greek).</note>. Concerning these kings, God said to Ahaz through the prophet:
>> "Do not fear, nor let your soul be weak because of these two wood-stumps, these two smoking firebrands." <note>Isaiah 7:4. A "firebrand" is a piece of burning wood; here it symbolizes kings whose power is nearly burned out.</note>

For having said that there would be an immediate and not long-delayed relief from these grievances, he goes on to prophesy that at the birth of God-with-us <note>original: μεθ' ἡμῶν... θεοῦ, a reference to the name "Emmanuel"</note>, both their kingdoms would be completely removed and destroyed. He shows from history that the leadership of both the Jews and the Damascenes lasted until the times of our Savior Jesus Christ. But after He appeared to all men, those kingdoms vanished in accordance with the prophecy, as the **Roman monarchy** <note>Eusebius often links the rise of the Roman Empire (the Pax Romana) with the spread of the Gospel, seeing both as divinely timed.</note> took control alongside the preaching of our Savior. 

When the Word had finished prophesying these things literally, He moved on to the deeper meaning—the more universal and spiritual application found in contemplation. He proposed two "swarms" <note>original: σίφη, often used for swarms of insects or troops</note> of invisible enemies and evil demons who wage war against the human race in different ways. One swarm works everywhere among men to promote idolatry and false doctrines; the other works to corrupt the character of souls. 

He demonstrates that the ruler of Damascus bears the image of the error of idolatry, while the ruler of Samaria is a type of those living a fallen, destructive, and materialistic life. He says the "land"—meaning the people dwelling on earth—would not be rid of these until Emmanuel, who is God, appeared on earth. Once He shone forth and began to reign over the human soul, none of those who formerly dominated it remained. This is why it is said here: 
>> "He shall take the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria." 

This happens as the power of our Savior Jesus Christ abolishes all the godless and invisible...

# PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, Book 7

...to our enemies, who long ago besieged all mankind with the godless and harmful activities previously mentioned. Specifically, concerning the birth and appearance of our Savior, it is said that the power of Damascus would be destroyed and the spoils of Samaria taken—meaning their kingdoms, which lasted until the times indicated but have ceased from then until now, according to the prophecies. Some offer another view: that the Magi who came from the East and worshiped Christ while he was a child are the "power of Damascus." You might also say more generally that all those who were formerly registered in godless and polytheistic idolatry but were brought into subjection by the word of Christ—especially those powerful in the word and wisdom of this age—are themselves called the "power of Damascus." You will understand the "spoils of Samaria" as the disciples and apostles of our Savior from the Jewish nation. Like spoils taken from enemies—those of the circumcision <note>original: ἐκ περιτομῆς; a term used for the Jewish people</note> who campaigned against him—he unexpectedly placed them under his own authority, replacing the things of the "King of the Assyrians." Here, the "King of Assyrians" is again used figuratively to mean the "Ruler of this Age" <note>original: ἄρχοντος τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου; a common early Christian term for the devil or worldly power opposed to God</note>.

> Since Aquila <note>A 2nd-century scholar who produced a literal Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible</note> rendered the reference to the King of the Assyrians more clearly, saying "in the presence of the King of the Assyrians," he indicates a situation that is not hostile but within the Roman borders. This is true if they are <unclear>hinting</unclear> at him, or if "Assyrians" is interpreted as "the one who is able," as was demonstrated a little earlier. Since the King of the Assyrians is now linked with the prophecy concerning our Savior, the Roman Empire is reasonably predicted here by us. Through this empire, he who came to earth for God brings about submission and service. For it says that the child being born will take the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria in the presence of the King of the Assyrians. It is prophesied that this will happen in the sight of those who lived according to the Law of God, and that he would do these things at the very time of his birth by an unutterable and divine power, while still being managed among men in an infant body. 

The prophet is commanded to record all these things on a "new scroll" and with a "man’s pen," signifying the word of the New Testament. He takes as witnesses to what was said a priest and a prophet, the Word teaching us that in our proofs concerning Christ, we must take testimonies from the priestly service in the Law and from the prophets who followed. He wants the witnesses to be faithful and worthy, who would be spectators of the birth of the child indicated, so they might understand what was prophesied. For "Unless you believe, you will not understand," as was said above. One witness we have is "Light of God"—for that is how "Uriah" is interpreted—and the other is a "Son of Blessing," or one who carries the "Memory of God" within himself, as "Zechariah son of Barachiah" signifies. 

These then are our insights into these passages. If any of the circumcision do not wish to accept these things as such, let them tell us, demonstrating who among them was ever "Emmanuel," and how the prophet approached the prophetess, and who she was, and how she immediately conceived, and who this son born of the prophetess was, to whom the Lord himself gave the name "Hasten-to-the-spoil, Quickly-take-the-prey" <note>The translation of the name Maher-shalal-hash-baz from Isaiah 8:3</note>, and what was the reason for such a name for the child? Let him explain...

The prophecy foretold that these kings would be overthrown at the birth of Emmanuel. Now, in a physical sense, during the days of Ahaz <note>A king of Judah in the 8th century BCE</note>, king of Judah, two kings according to the account of the prophet Isaiah entered a conspiracy to besiege the kingdoms of the successors of David, as has been shown before. One was the king of the idolatrous nations in Damascus, and the other was the king of the Jewish multitude in the city called Samaria in Palestine—which those in our time call Sebaste <note>The city was renamed Sebaste by Herod the Great in honor of Augustus Caesar (Sebastos in Greek)</note>. Concerning these kings, God said to Ahaz through the prophet:

> "Do not fear, and do not let your soul be faint because of these two smoldering stumps of firebrands."

Having said that the destruction of these men would happen very soon and not far off, the prophecy next foretells that at the birth of "God-with-us" <note>Emmanuel</note> who was to come, the kingdoms of both would be utterly extinguished and abolished. History shows that the set time for both the Jewish and Damascene kingdoms lasted until the times of our Savior Jesus Christ. But after His appearance to all mankind, they ceased in accordance with the prophecy, being replaced by the Roman Monarchy <note>original: Ῥωμαίων μοναρχίᾳ; referring to the Roman Empire's rise to sole power under Augustus</note> alongside the preaching of our salvation.

Having briefly completed this literal explanation, let us turn to the deeper meaning—the more universal and spiritual interpretation found in contemplation. Let us consider two hosts of invisible enemies and wicked demons who wage war against the entire human race in different ways: one group always works through idolatry and false doctrines among men, while the other group works through the corruption of morals in souls. The one representing the image of idolatrous error is the "Ruler of Damascus"; the one who is the type <note>In biblical interpretation, a "type" is a foreshadowing symbol</note> for those falling away from a temperate and healthy life is the "Ruler of Samaria." The prophecy says the "earth"—meaning the people dwelling on the earth—will not be rid of these until Emmanuel, God, appears on earth. When He shines forth and reigns over the human soul, none of those who formerly dominated it will remain. Thus, you will understand what is said here:

> "He will take the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria."

This refers to the power of our Savior Jesus Christ suddenly destroying all our invisible [enemies]...

### GOSPEL PROOF, Book 7

...since they were enemies, who long ago in ancient times besieged all humanity with the aforementioned godless and harmful activities. Regarding the literal sense of this specific passage, through the appearance of our Savior, the **power of Damascus** was cast down, and the **spoils of Samaria**—that is, their kingdoms, which had endured until the times indicated—quietly ceased from that point until the present, according to the prophecies.

Some say otherwise, that the **power of Damascus** refers to three Magi who came from the east and worshipped the child Christ. However, you might speak more generally: all those who turned away from godless and polytheistic idolatry and were brought into service to the word of Christ—especially if they were powerful in the speech and wisdom of this age—are themselves called the **power of Damascus**. 

And you will understand the **spoils of Samaria** as the disciples and apostles of our Savior from the Jewish nation. He took them as "spoils" from the enemy—or from the party of the circumcision <note>The Jewish community who adhered strictly to the Law</note> who campaigned against him—and disarmed them from the unbelief of the "foolish king," a term used metaphorically here for the **ruler of this age** <note>A common early Christian term for the Devil or the spirit of the world</note>.

Since <term>Aquila</term> <note>A 2nd-century translator of the Hebrew Bible into Greek, known for his literalism</note> rendered the phrase regarding the "king of the Assyrians" more clearly as "before the face of the king of the Assyrians," consider whether in these passages he also signifies the **Roman Empire**. This is because the name "Assyrians" can be interpreted as "those who direct" or "those who are directed," and matches the proofs we established a little earlier. 

Since the king of the Assyrians is now woven into the prophecy concerning our Savior, it is reasonable for us to understand the **Roman Empire** here; it is the means through which the work of God for the subjection of the nations is served. For the child being born, it says, will take the **power of Damascus** and the **spoils of Samaria** in a surrender "before the face of the Assyrians." This is prophesied in the eyes of those directed by God. He shall perform these things at the very time of his birth, through an ineffable and divine power, even while his body is still that of an infant—He who manages all things among men. 

The prophet is commanded to write all these things in a **large, new scroll** <note>Isaiah 8:1</note> (which is to be a human record), this being the "type" or foreshadowing of the New Testament. He also takes witnesses for these words: a priest and a prophet. By this, he teaches us that in providing proofs concerning Christ, we must take the testimony of the priestly service under the Law and the subsequent testimony of the prophets. He desires "faithful and simple witnesses" to be those who will proclaim the knowledge of the child, through which one can understand the things prophesied. "For if you do not believe, you will not understand," as was stated previously. 

But he who does not have the light of God—for this is how **Uriah** is interpreted—or the one who is a "son of blessing," carries the memory of God within himself. This is what **Zechariah** son of Berechiah signifies. 

We have elaborated on these points in their respective places. But if anyone from the circumcision <note>meaning Jewish scholars</note> does not wish to accept this interpretation, it is time for us to ask him: 

1. Who among them was ever an **Emmanuel**? 
2. How did the prophet "go to the prophetess," and who was she? 
3. How did she conceive immediately? 
4. And who is this son born to the prophetess, to whom the Lord himself gives the name **Swift-is-the-Spoil-Hasten-the-Prey**? <note>original: Ταχέως σκύλευσον, ὀξέως προνόμευσον (Maher-shalal-hash-baz)</note>

And who is shown to have set aside the names given to the child born of Isaiah...

He argues that the Magi and the Apostles represent the "spoils" taken from idolatry and unbelief.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Eusebius’s commentary on the Book of Isaiah. On the previous page, he interpreted the "power of Damascus" and the "spoils of Samaria" as symbols for the defeat of demonic forces and the conversion of the Gentiles following the birth of Christ. Here, he extends this interpretation to explain why the Jewish people faced national destruction by the Romans, linking historical events to the "softly flowing" waters of Siloam.</meta>

# EUSEBIUS #

...before the child knows how to call father and mother, he will have taken the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria in the presence of the king of the Assyrians. For we, taking these things both literally and figuratively, demonstrate that they were fulfilled at the birth of our Savior. We show that at one time we must apply the prophecies literally, according to their obvious meaning, and at another time <term>tropologically</term> <note>metaphorically or figuratively</note>. Immediately following the previously mentioned words, the prophecy adds further riddles:

> "And the Lord spoke to me again, saying: Because this people does not want the water of Siloam that flows softly, but instead wants to have Rezin and the son of Remaliah; for this reason, behold, the Lord brings up against you the water of the river, strong and many—the king of the Assyrians and his glory. And he shall rise up over every valley of yours, and shall walk over every wall of yours; and he shall take away from Judea every man who is able to raise his head or is able to accomplish anything. And his camp shall be so great as to fill the breadth of your land. God is with us! Know this, O nations, and be defeated; listen, even to the ends of the earth."

Clearly, these words preserve their true meaning only through <term>contemplation</term> <note>spiritual insight</note> and figurative interpretation. Indeed, by the "water of Siloam that flows softly," the prophecy signifies the Gospel teaching of the Word of Salvation. For the name **Siloam** is translated as "Sent." This would be the Word of God, sent to us from the Father, concerning whom Moses says:

> "A ruler shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until he comes for whom it is laid up; and he shall be the expectation of the nations." <note>Genesis 49:10</note>

The phrase "for whom it is laid up" in Hebrew contains the word **Siloam**. This indicates the same Siloam—that is, "the Sent One"—referenced in that passage. For some say the "king" represents those who were once idolaters in Damascus, just as the "son of Remaliah" represents those in Samaria among the Jewish people who revolted from their ancestral religion.

Therefore, God threatens those who did not accept Siloam—that is, the "Sent" Emmanuel—and the Son born of the Prophetess, nor his life-giving and fertile Word. Though this Word was brought forth clearly and gently, they rejected it. Instead, they brought upon themselves either the rulers of the idolatrous nations or the spirit of apostasy. For this reason, God will bring against them the "strong and many water of the river," which the word of prophecy immediately interprets, saying it is the **king of the Assyrians**. 

Again, according to the figurative sense, this signifies the **ruler of this age** <note>The Devil</note>, or the current empire of the Romans. Those who rejected the "softly flowing water of Siloam" were handed over to these powers, having subjected themselves to doctrines that are contrary and hostile to the right Word. 

Thus, immediately and not long after they failed to receive the Gospel of our Savior and rejected the drink of Siloam that flows softly, the Roman army—guided by God—came upon them. They rose up over every one of their valleys and walked over every one of their walls. They took away from Judea every man who was able to raise his head or accomplish anything. The "camp" of those described became so great that it filled the breadth of the entire land of Judea. This was fulfilled literally in their experience. If you wish to learn the reason why this happened, listen: it is because **Emmanuel**, "God is with us," has come.

<summary>Eusebius interprets the "water of Siloam" as the "Sent" Word of God (Christ) and argues that the Roman conquest of Judea was a divine consequence of the Jewish people rejecting the gentle Gospel in favor of worldly or apostate powers.</summary>

# THE PROOF OF THE GOSPEL #
## Book 7 ##

-> **EVANGELICAL PROOF. Book 7** <-

...Emmanuel, who was born from our nature, but was not "with them" <note>The Jewish people</note>. For if they had held onto Him, they would not have suffered these things. Therefore, the Word cries out next to the nations concerning Emmanuel, saying: "God is with us! Know this, O nations, and be defeated." <note>Isaiah 8:8-9. Eusebius emphasizes that "God with us" is the translation of the name "Emmanuel."</note> These things are interpreted among us; one might say that it is necessary to understand the majority of prophecies sometimes literally, and sometimes through riddles <note>Original: <foreign>ainigmon</foreign>; referring to allegorical or symbolic meanings</note>. From this starting point, it is appropriate to examine the rest of the prophecy at hand in a similar way.

If anyone even now seeks these things for some future time—as those "of the circumcision" <note>The Jewish people</note> claim regarding their expected Messiah, anticipating that these things will happen strictly and literally—they must be asked: How will the one who has not yet come (according to them) take the "power of Damascus" and the "spoils of Samaria" in the presence of the "king of the Assyrians"? For Samaria has already been destroyed at the present time and no longer exists; nor does the name of the "power of Damascus" exist in any way, nor the dynasty of the Assyrians, which the Medes and Persians overthrew and succeeded long ago. Since none of these entities even exist at the present time, how is it possible to expect their destruction in a future time?

Furthermore, one cannot say that the things prophesied happened at some other point in the distant past. No one among the Hebrews was ever born of a prophetess mother and Isaiah the prophet who routed the "spoils of Samaria" and the "power of Damascus" against the king of the Assyrians, as if it were a recorded literal history. 

Thus, one must absolutely confess that these things were fulfilled only according to the interpretation we have given—namely, during the first appearance of Jesus our Savior, in whom we have demonstrated that the foretold events reached their fulfillment. According to the prophecy, the "new volume" <note>Original: <foreign>kainos tomos</foreign>; a reference to Isaiah 8:1</note> was also written at that same appearance; this is the message of the New Testament, which contains the "tongue" of the Prophetess's son. By an unspeakable and divine power, He handed over the royal power of Damascus and all Syria—which are interpreted for us as the "spoils of Samaria"—into the hands of the Roman Empire. 

Moreover, in a spiritual sense, He took His disciples from among the Jews as a kind of "spoils," surrounding them with mental and rational weapons. He set them against the face of the aforementioned "king of the Assyrians" <note>Eusebius often uses "Assyrians" to symbolize demonic forces or the spiritual "enemy"</note>, and prepared them as His own specialized soldiers.

But as for those who were disobedient to the fertile and life-giving water of His teaching—which "flows softly" <note>A reference to the waters of Siloam from Isaiah 8:6</note>—and who stir up warlike things hostile to God, He delivered them to the "king of the Assyrians," to whom they remain enslaved even now. He truly "rose up over every valley of theirs and over every wall of yours," and He removed from Judea every ruler and king called a "head," and every powerful man was brought to an end. 

Consequently, from that time until now, they have possessed neither a "head" <note>A leader or sovereign</note> nor any powerful man in divine matters, such as those who once excelled among them—whether a prophet or a man altogether righteous and beloved by God. It is evident how even now their whole country remains subject to their enemies and foes, and how all these things were accomplished at the appearance of Emmanuel. For so the Hebrew scripture contains it, almost signifying that Emmanuel, though disbelieved by the Jews...

# EUSEBIUS #

...and he was the cause of so many calamities that befell them <note>The Jewish people who rejected him</note>, but for us from the nations who have believed, he has been shown to be the author of salvation and the knowledge of God. Therefore, it follows next: "God is with us; know, O nations, and be defeated." <note>Isaiah 8:8-9</note> We, then, who are from the nations and have believed in Him, have truly been "defeated," conquered by the truth and by the power of the God who has become "with us." Having been defeated, we have all together become His subjects—even those dwelling to the ends of the earth, according to the prophecy saying: "Listen, even to the end of the earth." <note>Isaiah 8:9</note>

Thus, while we have been defeated and have rightly obeyed, the Word directs the following to those who still disobey the straight path, saying: "Though you have grown strong, you shall be defeated. For if you should grow strong again, again you shall be defeated. And whatever counsel you take, it shall not stand among you, because God is with us." <note>Isaiah 8:9-10</note> Thus says the Lord to those who disobey with a strong hand. Through these words, the Word clearly marks out those who set themselves in opposition to the teaching of Christ and those who disobey His mighty hand. It foretells that they will not even have the strength to wage war against the God who is "with us" <note>Original: <foreign>meth’ hēmōn theos</foreign>, the translation of Emmanuel</note> and that whatever they plan against us will not remain with them, because Emmanuel is with us. With this conclusion, it is easy to observe the threats made against us and the uprisings during the times of the rulers; one sees how the outcome of their threats is always rendered futile because of "God with us."

How the prophesied Son, born from the prophesied woman—whether a virgin or a young maiden—is proclaimed as both God and the "Angel of Great Counsel," along with other wondrous titles. Also, how His birth will be established as the cause of the light of piety for the nations.

"Drink this first. Do it quickly." <note>Isaiah 9:1. To which he adds: "For every garment gathered by deceit, and every robe with exchange, they shall repay; and they shall wish if they had been burnt with fire, because a child was born to us and a son was given to us, whose government is upon his shoulder. The zeal of the Lord of Hosts shall do these things." <note>Isaiah 9:6-7</note>

This is now the third child prophesied, or rather, the same child being signified in various ways. Since our purpose now is to show the manner of God's presence among men—through how many means and how it was provided—He was first shown as the one called Emmanuel, God being born of a virgin. Second, He was shown as the child born from the prophetess through the Holy Spirit, not being different from the one previously mentioned. Third, the child now at hand is one and the same as the previous ones. He is said to have these names—especially according to the Seventy <term>The "Seventy" refers to the Septuagint (LXX), the standard Greek translation of the Old Testament used by the early Church</term>—such as "Angel of Great Counsel," so that...

> » [Or another] copy has: Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Potentate, Prince of Peace, Father of the Age to Come. <note>These are titles from Isaiah 9:6. Eusebius is noting a variant reading in the Septuagint manuscripts.</note> According to the Hebrew, as **Aquila** <note>A 2nd-century Jewish proselyte who produced a literal Greek translation of the Old Testament.</note> says: "For a child has been born to us, a son has been given to us, and the measure <note>Original: *metron*. In the Hebrew text, this refers to 'government' or 'rule.'</note> was upon his shoulder. And his name was called: Wonderful Counselor, Strong, Mighty, Father, and even Prince of Peace, and of his peace there is no end." And as **Symmachus** <note>Another 2nd-century translator who aimed for more elegant Greek than Aquila.</note> says: "For a youth has been given to us, a son has been given to us. And his discipline <note>Original: *paideia*. Usually translated as 'government' in this context, but Symmachus uses a word related to education or training.</note> shall be upon his shoulder, and his name shall be called: An Extraordinary Honor, Counseling, Strong, Mighty, Father of the Age, Prince of Peace, and of his peace there is no end." Therefore, he is not simply an "angel" according to the **Seventy** <note>The Septuagint (LXX), the standard Greek translation used by the early Church.</note>,

but the "Angel of Great Counsel," and "Wonderful Counselor," and "Mighty God" and "Potentate," and "Prince of Peace," and "Father of the Age to Come." Through these titles, it is promised that he will be born and will be a child. You have in the preceding sections One who was proclaimed in various ways as "God the Word," both "God" and "Lord," but who was at the same time named the "Angel of the Father" and the "Captain of the Host of the Lord." <note>Eusebius identifies the figure in Isaiah with the "Logos" (the Word) who appeared in the Old Testament as the Angel of the Lord.</note> Who, then, could this be who—according to Aquila and the testimonies still carried among the Hebrews today—is born among men and becomes a child, yet is "Wonderful Counselor" and "Strong," "Mighty," and "Father," and even "Prince of Peace," of whose peace he says there shall never be an end? And according to Symmachus, he is "An Extraordinary Honor," "Counseling," "Strong," "Mighty," "Father of the Age," "Prince of Peace," and this peace is infinite and endless. And according to **Theodotion** <note>A 2nd-century translator whose work often revised the Septuagint toward the Hebrew.</note>: "Wonderfully Counseling, Mighty Potentate, Father, Prince of Peace, by the multiplying of discipline." Of whose peace there is no end.

It is for you and for others to consider this, noting this point: that this very person who is called "Father of the Age" and "Prince of Infinite Peace" and "Angel of Great Counsel" is prophesied to be born and to be a child. Furthermore, at his presence among men, those who are envious of the salvation of the nations achieved through him—whether they be evil demons or impious 

> » men—shall wish for things to be "burned with fire." <note>A reference to Isaiah 9:5, describing the destruction of the enemies' gear.</note> Concerning these men he says: "Every garment gathered by deceit, and the robe [taken] with a trade-off, they shall repay." <note>Eusebius is using a variant of the Greek text for Isaiah 9:5.</note> Thus shall they be overpowered; or as it is said elsewhere concerning his person, or rather our Savior: "They divided my garments among themselves, and for my clothing they cast lots." <note>Psalm 22:18 (LXX 21:19), famously applied to the crucifixion.</note> Those who share in their impiety will wish [for this], 

later seeing their own judgment, if the fire generated by their own impiety is "burned with fire" before the Angel of Great Counsel was present to be treated impiously. <note>Eusebius suggests the "fire" of judgment is sparked by the very sins of those who reject Christ.</note> And you should consider for yourself whether it is not beyond all human nature for his peace to be said to have "no end," and for him to be named "Father of the Age." Consider also that even among those [translators] he is not simply an "angel," but "Angel of Great Counsel," and "Mighty God," and all the other titles listed with these. Furthermore, he says that the Kingdom of David shall be set right through him. You should understand this in the following way: very many promises were made to David, in which

> » it was said: "I will set his hand in the sea, and his right hand in the rivers. He shall call upon me, saying, 'You are my Father, my God, and the helper of my salvation.' And I will make him my firstborn, high above the kings of the earth. I will keep my mercy for him forever, and my covenant shall be faithful to him. And I will establish his seed for ever and ever, and his throne as the days of heaven." And again: "Once I have sworn by my holiness, I will not lie to David: his seed shall endure forever..." <note>Psalm 89:25-36 (LXX 88:26-37).</note>

# EUSEBIUS #

» "his throne, and his throne as the sun before me, and as the moon established for the age." <note>Quoting Psalm 89:36–37 (Psalm 88 in the Septuagint numbering).</note> Since these things were promised by God concerning David in the Psalms, it happened that very different circumstances befell these promises because of the impieties of David's successors. At any rate, the kingdom from the seed of David, having lasted until the time of Jeconiah and the siege of the Temple by the Babylonians, was dissolved, so that from that point on, neither the throne of David nor those of his seed ruled over the Jewish nation. And this specific failure of the promise made to David—according to the comparison set forth in the prophesied Psalm—the Divine Spirit foretells in this way: » "But You have cast off and brought to nothing, You have put off Your Christ; <note>Original: *christon sou*. In the Greek Old Testament, this term refers to the "anointed" king of Israel, but Eusebius interprets the "putting off" as the temporary suspension of the Davidic line until the coming of Jesus the Christ.</note> You have overturned the covenant of Your servant, You have profaned his sanctuary to the ground. You have broken down all his hedges." » And a little later: "What has happened to him You have dashed to the ground, You have shortened the days of his time, You have poured shame upon him." These events, which clearly began to be fulfilled from the Babylonian captivity of the people, extended until the reign of the Romans and Tiberius. For no one from the line of David appears to have sat upon the royal throne of the Hebrew nation in the intervening times, until the arrival of Christ. But when our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, the leader from the seed of David, was proclaimed King over the whole inhabited world, that very throne of David was renewed, as if from the ground and from its fall; through our Savior, He became King of men like the sun, and He shall remain for the age. Even now, like the sun before God, He illuminates the whole inhabited world with the rays of the light of His teaching, in accordance with the message of the Psalm and the prophecy at hand. The prophecy speaks of the child to be born, saying that he will establish "the throne of David"—that is, the eternal and lasting throne—which was promised to David, to set him upon his kingdom, to order it and to support it with judgment and justice from now and forever. As to how these things were fulfilled, the angel Gabriel would be a trustworthy teacher in his message to the Virgin, saying: » "Do not fear, Mary, for you have found favor with God. And behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you will call his name Jesus. He will be great and will be called the Son of the Highest, and the Lord God will give him the throne of his father David, and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end." » Therefore, the prophet, looking forward to this birth of Christ prophesied in the Psalm—considering both its substance and the delay as the cause of the fall of David's throne—laments, saying: » "But You have cast off and brought to nothing, You have put off Your Christ." » He was, as it were, entreating the Divine to quickly fulfill the promises, saying: » "Where are Your ancient mercies, O Lord, which You swore to David in Your truth?" » He foretells that these very things will be most clearly fulfilled upon the birth of the "Angel of Great Counsel." <note>The Septuagint's title for the child in Isaiah 9:6.</note> Rejoicing in this, he says that those previously given up to be "burned with fire" <note>Referring to the judgment described in Isaiah 9:5.</note> were ransomed, "because a child was born to us, and a son was given to us, the Angel of Great Counsel." For whom? For us? Or for those who believed in Him in "Galilee of the Gentiles"? To whom He became the cause of light and joy, and of a new... <note>Text cuts off; Eusebius is beginning to describe the New Covenant.</note>

# THE PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, BOOK 7 #

### 211 ###

> » "...drink this first, do it quickly. <note>original: *πρῶτον πίε, ταχὺ ποίη* (proton pie, tachy poiei). This phrase from the Septuagint version of Isaiah 9:1 is obscure; modern translations usually render the Hebrew as "he humbled the land." Eusebius follows the Greek version available to him.</note> O land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, and the rest who dwell by the seacoast, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles. O people sitting in darkness, see a great light! And for those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death, a light has dawned upon them." <note>Quoting Isaiah 9:1–2. These regions in northern Israel were the first to be invaded by Assyria, but here they are promised the first glimpse of the Messiah's light.</note>

These verses might signify those from the nations <note>The "nations" or "Gentiles" refers to non-Jewish people who would eventually embrace Christianity.</note> who have believed in the Christ of God, as well as the disciples and apostles of our Savior. He called them from the land of Zebulun and Naphtali and chose them as heralds of the Gospel. To these, then, the "Angel of Great Counsel" was given as a Son, the cause of salvation; but to those who were disobedient toward him, he became a cause of fire and burning. He [the prophet] says the motive for this entire <term>economy</term> <note>original: *oikonomia*. In early Christian writing, this refers to God's "plan" or "arrangement" for human salvation through Christ.</note> was the "zeal of the Lord," saying: "The zeal of the Lord of Hosts shall do this." What kind of zeal? Perhaps that which Moses mentions, saying: "They have made me jealous with that which is no god; they have provoked me to anger with their idols. And I will make them jealous with those who are not a nation; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation." <note>Quoting Deuteronomy 32:21. Eusebius suggests God's "zeal" involves turning to the Gentiles because Israel turned to idols.</note>

Indeed, since the Father and the Son’s loving-kindness in his visitation to humanity has been shown, and the very place of his appearance has been demonstrated through the prophetic testimonies, it is time to see where on earth he was to be born, from where he would come, and from which Hebrew tribe it was proclaimed he would proceed. Let us search these things out as well.

---

### Concerning the place of the birth of the God who was proclaimed. From Micah. ###

How from Bethlehem, a place in Palestine, one pre-existing from eternity, a leader of the race of the godly, shall come forth; and how the Lord himself is prophesied to shepherd those who have believed in him to the ends of the earth.

> **A**nd you, Bethlehem, house of Ephrathah, are few to be among the thousands of Judah. From you shall come forth for me a leader, to be a ruler in Israel. And his goings forth <note>original: *exodoi*. This term suggests his origins or his acts of "coming out."</note> are from the beginning, from the days of eternity. Therefore he shall give them up until the time she who is in labor has given birth. Then the rest of his brothers shall return to the sons of Israel. And he shall stand and see, and shall shepherd his flock in the strength of the Lord, and they shall exist in the glory of the name of the Lord their God. Because now they shall be magnified to the ends of the earth, and this one shall be... <note>Quoting Micah 5:2–4 (Micah 5:1-3 in the Septuagint).</note>

...this peace." Immanuel—which is translated as "God with us"—was clearly shown through what was set out before as not being born from a mortal, but becoming a child, being the "Angel of Great Counsel." <note>Eusebius connects the "child" of Isaiah 9:6 with the "ruler" from Bethlehem in Micah 5:2.</note> But it was also necessary that the place of his birth be signaled. Thus, it prophesies that a ruler in Israel shall come forth from Bethlehem, having his "goings forth" from the beginning, from the days of eternity. This would not fit human nature, except only for Immanuel and the "Angel of Great Counsel." For to whom else would "subsisting from eternity" apply, if not to God alone? 

Therefore, from Bethlehem (which is a place in Judea, not far from Jerusalem), it is said that one existing from eternity shall come forth. We need not seek another than him whom we knew was shown to David as born, and then after him our Savior Jesus, the Christ of God. No one other than these. For David, having preceded the times of the prophecy, had died many years before the prediction. Nor were his "goings forth" from the days of eternity. Therefore, it remains to apply this to the one who was born in Bethlehem after these things, who is clearly Immanuel, who existed before all creation.

<summary>Eusebius interprets Isaiah's prophecy of Galilee and Micah's prophecy of Bethlehem as proofs of Christ's divine nature and geographic origin. He argues that the phrase "from the days of eternity" can only refer to a pre-existent God, not a mere human ruler like David.</summary>

» "...his seed shall endure forever, and his throne as the sun before me, and as the moon established forever." <note>original: *σπέρμα αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα μενεῖ* (sperma autou eis ton aiōna menei). Quoting Psalm 89:36–37 (LXX 88:37–38).</note> He [the Psalmist] says in the Psalms that these things were promised to the seed of David; yet it certainly happened that the opposite of these promises came to pass because of the impiety of his successors. Indeed, the kingdom from the seed of David, which lasted until the time of Jeconiah <note>Jeconiah, also known as Jehoiachin, was one of the last kings of Judah before the Babylonian Captivity (c. 597 BCE).</note> and the siege of the Temple by the Babylonians, was dissolved. From that time on, the throne of David no longer existed, nor did any of his descendants reign over the Jewish nation. This very collapse of the promise made to David is what the Divine Spirit foretells through the prophecy in the Psalm, speaking in this way: "But you have cast off and abhorred, you have rejected your Christ; <note>The word *Christos* here refers to the "Anointed One" or the Davidic king.</note> you have overthrown the covenant of your servant, you have profaned his sanctuary to the ground; you have broken down all his hedges." And shortly after: "You have cast down his throne to the ground, you have shortened the days of his time, you have poured shame upon him." 

These events clearly began to be fulfilled from the time of the people’s captivity in Babylon and extended until the reign of the Romans and Tiberius. <note>Tiberius Caesar was the Roman Emperor during the ministry of Jesus.</note> For no one from the lineage of David appears to have sat upon the royal throne of the Hebrew nation during the intervening years until the presence of Christ. But when our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, who is of the seed of David, was proclaimed King over the entire world, that very throne of David—as if renewed from the earth and its ruins—was raised up again through our Savior's divine kingdom, and it shall remain forever. Even now, it shines like the sun before God, illuminating the whole inhabited world with the rays of the light of his teaching. 

Consequently, following the memorial in the Psalm, the prophecy currently at hand <note>Referring to Isaiah 9:6–7.</note> speaks concerning the child to be born, saying that he would establish the throne of David as eternal and enduring—the very one promised to David—restoring his kingdom and upholding it with judgment and righteousness from this time forth and forever. 

As to how these things were fulfilled, the Angel Gabriel would be a worthy teacher in his announcement to the Virgin, saying: "Do not fear, Mary, for you have found favor with God. And behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus. He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High, and the Lord God will give to him the throne of David his father, and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end." <note>Quoting the Annunciation from Luke 1:30–33.</note> 

The prophet, anticipating this birth of Christ in the prophetic Psalm, and seeing both its substance and its "delay" <note>The "delay" or "postponement" refers to the long gap between the earthly kings and Christ.</note> as the cause for the falling away of David's throne, laments, saying: "But you have cast off and abhorred, you have rejected your Christ." He prays that the divine promises might be fulfilled quickly, saying: "Where are your ancient mercies, O Lord, which you swore to David in your truth?" These very things are most clearly prophesied to be fulfilled on the day of the "Angel of Great Counsel." <note>original: *Μεγάλης Βουλῆς Ἄγγελος* (Megales Boules Angelos). This is the Septuagint's translation of the titles in Isaiah 9:6, which English Bibles usually render as "Wonderful Counselor."</note> Regarding this, he says those who were previously led to be burned were gladdened because they were ransomed: "For unto us a child is born, and unto us a son is given," the Angel of Great Counsel. For "us"—those who have believed in him in Galilee of the Gentiles—he has become the cause of light and joy, and of something new among the nations: the mystery of the New Covenant, according to the prophecy that said, this first...

<summary>Eusebius explains that the "throne of David," which appeared lost after the Babylonian exile, is eternally restored through the spiritual and global kingship of Jesus Christ. He links the lament of Psalm 89 to the fulfillment announced by the Angel Gabriel and the prophecy of Isaiah 9.</summary>

> How it was prophesied that from Bethlehem, a place in Palestine, one who pre-exists from eternity would come as a leader of the godly; and how the Lord himself is divinely foretold as shepherding those who have believed in him even to the ends of the earth.

# EUSEBIUS #

<margin>Eusebius, Preparation for the Gospel</margin>

>> He says that he will rule all people even to the ends of the earth. It says, therefore: "And he shall stand, and shall see, and shall shepherd his flock in the strength of the Lord, and in the glory of the name of the Lord their God they shall exist; for now they shall be magnified unto the ends of the earth, and this shall be peace." <note>original: Micah 5:4. Eusebius interprets the 'magnification' of the flock as the spread of Christianity.</note>

For whom shall this peace be, if not for the earth in which the flocks of the Lord shall be magnified? The kind of fulfillment this met after the coming of our Savior Jesus Christ is completely obvious to everyone. For whereas before this there was much <term>polyarchy: original "polyarchia," referring to a world divided into many small kingdoms, city-states, and tribal territories</term> "rule by many," and all nations were ruled by tyrants or democracies, there was no interaction among men. For instance, the Egyptians were ruled by their own leader, as were the Arabs, the Idumaeans, the Phoenicians, the Syrians, and other nations. Nations were rising against nations, and cities against cities, with countless sieges and captivities taking place in every spot and region. 

But when the Savior and Lord appeared—coinciding with his arrival among men and on the occasion of Augustus <note>Gaius Julius Caesar Octavianus (Augustus), the first Roman Emperor, whose reign began the Pax Romana.</note> the Roman gaining mastery over the nations—the "rule by many" was mostly dissolved. Peace took hold of the entire earth, in accordance with the prophecy at hand, which explicitly said concerning the disciples of Christ: "For now they shall be magnified unto the ends of the earth, and this shall be peace." With this the Psalm also agrees, speaking an oracle about Christ: "In his days righteousness shall spring up, and abundance of peace." <note>original: Psalm 72:7 (71:7 in the LXX). Eusebius views the political stability of Rome as a divine tool for the Gospel's spread.</note> 

Therefore, it seems to me he is named the "Ruler of Peace" in this perfect prophecy, since the prophet at hand said that the Lord would come forth from the heavens—not just to shepherd men, or be born in Bethlehem, but specifically to be in Bethlehem. <note>Eusebius is emphasizing that the prophecy isn't just about a general appearance, but a specific geographical fulfillment.</note> How these things were brought to fulfillment in our Savior and Lord, the Evangelist <note>The Gospel writer, likely referring to Matthew or Luke mentioned in previous sections.</note> bore witness through the voices we set out before. 

Christ is said to be shown as a shepherd and leader to "Israel," as Holy Scripture is accustomed to applying the name "true Israelites" in mind to all those who practice a healing and virtuous life. Conversely, it calls those of the circumcision <term>circumcision: a common shorthand in early Christian writing for the Jewish people</term>—whenever they are unholy—"Canaanites," "seed of Chanaan and not of Judah," "rulers of Sodom," and "people of Gomorrah," naming them after deeds that resemble theirs. 

Generally speaking, in a literal sense, the entire ministry of our Savior took place among the Jewish nation, and he led many of Israel—at least those who knew him and believed in him from among the circumcision. And the prophecy that was fulfilled took this sort of outcome. But what follows from the start of another reading is as follows:

>> "And the Assyrian, when he comes upon your land, and when he treads upon your country, then there shall be raised up against him seven shepherds, and eight bites <note>original: δήγματα (dēgmata). In the Septuagint, this word means 'bites' or 'stings,' though modern translations of the Hebrew usually read 'leaders' or 'princes.'</note> of men," 

and the things following these. What meaning these things hold is not for the present time to describe. One might say that after the Assyrian arrival in Judea, in which they took the Jewish nation, as many uprisings occurred against them as are shown through the seven shepherds and the eight "bites." Those who have researched the history of the Assyrians might know these things, at the end of which the one prophesied from Bethlehem appeared. The seven shepherds and the eight bites clearly happen to the Assyrians in times later than their invasion of Judea. But as these things require much investigation, now is not the time for meddling.
