As the seventy-year captivity of the Jewish nation in Babylon was already drawing to a close, the archangel Gabriel appeared to Daniel while he was praying. Gabriel prophesied the renewal of Jerusalem, stating it would happen immediately and not in the distant future. He also limited the time of the city’s subsequent enjoyment of peace to a specific number of years. He foretold that after this fixed deadline, it would again be cast down. Having endured this second capture and siege, it would no longer receive oversight from God but would remain a desert. Along with the city, the worship according to the Law of Moses would be abolished, and in its place, a New Covenant would be introduced to the lives of men. Gabriel reveals these things to the prophet in a hidden, oracular manner. He says to Daniel: "I have now come forth to give you insight; at the beginning of your supplication the word went out, and I have come to tell you, for you are a man of desires; therefore, consider the word and understand the vision." By this, he clearly rouses him to a deeper perception and understanding of the theories being discussed. He calls these things a "vision" precisely because they require a deeper mind and more than just ordinary intelligence. Therefore, to the prophet himself—

<meta>This page continues Eusebius's detailed breakdown of the "Seventy Weeks" in Daniel 9, shifting from the text itself to a linguistic and historical analysis of why the angel Gabriel uses specific phrasing when addressing Daniel. Eusebius argues that the prophecy predicts a specific 490-year window ending with the arrival of Christ and the Roman takeover of Judea.</meta>

<page-num>238</page-num>

-> EUSEBIUS <-

...insight for men, and having called upon Him that the eyes of our understanding might be enlightened by Him, let us investigate the contemplation of the passages concerning Him.

> “Seventy,” he says, “weeks have been decreed <note>original: "συνετμήθησαν"—literally "cut short," "shortened," or "apportioned." Eusebius uses this to imply a strictly limited timeframe.</note> for your people, and for your holy city, to finish sin, and to wipe away lawlessness, and to make atonement for iniquities, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal vision and prophecy, and to anoint the Holy of Holies.”

It is clear to everyone that the period of seventy weeks, when counted in years, brings together a number of four hundred and ninety years. This amount of time, therefore, was "decreed" for your people—a conclusion that encompasses the entire Jewish nation. He no longer addresses them as God’s people, but says to Daniel, "your people." 

Just as when they once acted impiously and practiced idolatry in the wilderness, God no longer called them His own people, but spoke to Moses, saying: "Go, go down; for **your people** have acted lawlessly." I believe the angel here teaches the same thing regarding the limited time defined for them: that they are no longer deemed worthy to be called the people of God. He adds, “and for the holy city.” This is to be understood in the same way, as if he were saying: "for your people, and for your holy city," or as if he said, "the city that was *considered* holy." 

The Hebrew text, and the other translators in agreement, include "your" not only for the people but also for the city. For instance, Aquila <note>Aquila of Sinope was a 2nd-century translator known for his extremely literal Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible.</note> says: "for your people, and for your sanctified city." And Symmachus <note>Symmachus the Ebionite was a late 2nd-century translator who aimed for more elegant Greek than Aquila.</note> says: "against your people, and your holy city." Therefore, in the accurate copies of the Septuagint <note>The standard Greek version of the Old Testament.</note>, we will find the word "your" [σου] added with an asterisk.

For when Daniel prayed, in the words of his supplications, he repeatedly called the people "the people of God" and the site of the city "the holy place of God." But the one giving the divine response <note>The angel Gabriel.</note> turns this around; he no longer acknowledges either the city as the "holy city of God" nor the people as the "people of God," but says "yours"—referring to you who are praying and who said such things about the people and the place and the city. 

Daniel’s words were as follows:

> “Let your anger and your wrath be turned away from your city Jerusalem, your holy mountain... and your people have become a reproach among all those around us.” 
>
> And again: “Cause your face to shine upon your sanctuary which is desolate.” 
>
> And further: “Look upon the vanishing of your city, upon which your name has been called.” 
>
> And following this: “Because your name was called upon your city and upon your people.” 

While Daniel was saying these things, and “while I was still speaking and praying,” behold, Gabriel, whom I had seen in my vision, flying, touched me and spoke to me the things written above.

Clearly, through these words, the prophet did not simply name the city, but called it "God's city," and the sanctuary "God's sanctuary," and the people "God's people." But because of the coming break with the people, Gabriel no longer calls these things by the same names as Daniel did. Instead, he says, “for **your** people,” and “for **your** holy city,” almost as if he were declaring the city and the people to be unworthy of being called God's own. 

He teaches that this specific amount of time was limited first regarding the people, and then regarding the city. This duration is shown to be from the restoration of Jerusalem—which occurred under Darius, the King of the Persians—until the Roman dominion under Augustus, and Herod, who was king of the Jews but a foreigner by race <term>Herod the Great was an Idumaean; Eusebius highlights this to show that the scepter had departed from Judah as prophesied in Genesis 49:10</term>. It is under these rulers that the birth of our Savior is recorded, as the argument will demonstrate as it proceeds.

He identifies the 490-year prophecy as spanning from the reign of Darius the Persian to the time of Augustus and Herod.</summary>

...stration. Next, he adds: "to finish sin, and to seal up sin, and to wipe away lawlessness, and to make atonement for iniquities, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal vision and prophet, and to anoint the Holy of Holies." 

Instead of "to finish sin and to seal up sin," Aquila <note>Aquila of Sinope was a 2nd-century Jewish convert and translator known for his extremely literal Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible.</note> has rendered it: "to complete the rebellion <note>original: "ἀθεσία"—this term implies a "setting aside" of God’s law or a revolt against His authority.</note> and to finish sin." 

For the phrase "Fill up the measure of your fathers," spoken by our Savior to the people of the circumcision <note>A common early Christian term for the Jewish people, referring to the covenant of Abraham.</note>, is, I believe, represented through these words. For in the plot dared against Him by the Jewish nation, their sin was "finished," and their "rebellion" against God (according to Aquila) reached its completion. 

For long ago, God's long-suffering patience bore with them, despite their many offenses before the coming of our Savior, as is shown through the prophetic words I mentioned earlier. But just as it was said to Abraham regarding the foreigners who formerly inhabited the Promised Land: "For the sins of the Amorites are not yet full" (Genesis 15:16); and as long as they were not yet full, the Amorites were not yet driven from their ancestral land. But when their sins were filled, then they were all destroyed in the time of Joshua <note>original: "Ἰησοῦ"—In Greek, the names "Jesus" and "Joshua" are identical. Eusebius is referring to the biblical successor of Moses.</note>, the successor of Moses. 

You should understand the case of the Jewish people in the same way. For as long as their sins were not full, God’s forbearance and long-suffering bore with them, calling them to return at every opportunity through the prophets. But when, according to the Savior's voice, they "filled up the measure of their fathers," all their deeds gathered against Him brought about their final destruction. This is just as our Lord Himself teaches again, saying: "All the blood shed from the foundation of the world, from the blood of Abel the righteous to the blood of Zechariah... shall come upon this generation" (Matthew 23:35-36). 

So, by daring at the very last to lay hands on the Son of God, they "completed the rebellion" and "finished their own sin," according to Aquila’s translation. According to the Seventy <note>The Septuagint, the most widely used Greek translation of the Old Testament in the early Church.</note>, their sin was "given and sealed." 

But since He came not only "for the fall" but also "for the rising of many in Israel," as it says of Him: "Behold, this child is set for the fall and rising of many in Israel," it is fitting that Daniel adds to what was said: "and to wipe away sins, and to make atonement for iniquities." 

For since it was "impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins," it was necessary to show clearly that the specific atonement for men belongs to the Living and True [God], of which the "mercy-seat" <note>original: "ἱλαστήριον"—the gold lid of the Ark of the Covenant, where the High Priest sprinkled blood on the Day of Atonement.</note> constructed by Moses was a type. And this is our Savior and Lord, the Lamb of God, concerning whom it is said: "Behold, the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world" (John 1:29). And again: "He is the atonement <note>original: "ἱλασμός"—propitiation or a sacrifice that brings reconciliation.</note> for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the whole world." 

He Himself is also "redemption," as Paul says: "who became for us wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification and redemption." Appropriately, then, the prophecy teaches that His presence was both the "filling up" and "completion of sin" for those who acted impiously toward Him, and at the same time the "wiping away" and "cleansing of sins" and "atonement for iniquities" for those who have believed in Him. 

And Aquila, having said "to complete the rebellion and to finish the sin," added "to make atonement for lawlessness," clearly suggesting that He Himself is the atonement for every lawlessness previously committed in ignorance. Following these things it is said: "to...

» "...to bring in everlasting righteousness." This is indeed the Word of God Himself, the **everlasting righteousness**, who became for us "wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification and redemption," according to the Apostle <note>Referring to Paul in 1 Corinthians 1:30.</note>. Furthermore, He brought forth the righteousness inherent in Himself among all men, showing by His works that God is not only the God of the Jews, but also of the Gentiles; since "God is one, who will justify the circumcision by faith and the uncircumcision through faith" <note>Romans 3:29-30.</note>. 

» Hence, Peter, marveling at those around Cornelius <note>Cornelius was a Roman centurion and the first Gentile convert; his story in Acts 10 marks the expansion of the Gospel beyond Judaism.</note> who were deemed worthy of the Holy Spirit, said: "In truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons, but in every nation whoever fears Him and works righteousness is acceptable to Him." And Paul says the Gospel is one of righteousness, saying: "For it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek. For in it the righteousness of God is revealed." 

» In the Psalms also it is said of Christ: "In his days shall righteousness flourish, and abundance of peace" <note>Psalm 72:7.</note>. By manifesting Himself, He truly displayed the righteousness of God, having deemed every race of men equally worthy of the divine calling. 

» But the things given through Moses were not like this, being granted to the Jewish nation alone. Therefore, having appeared for a season, they have passed away. But the righteousness proclaimed through our Savior, remaining forever, was rightly called **everlasting righteousness**, according to Gabriel who said, "and to bring in everlasting righteousness."

» Instead of the phrase, "and to seal vision and prophet," it seems to me that Aquila <note>Aquila was a 2nd-century translator known for his literalism; Eusebius often prefers his word choices for technical clarity.</note> has used a more precise term, saying, "**and to complete** <term>original: τελέσαι — to finish, fulfill, or bring to an end</term> **vision and prophet**." 

» For our Savior and Lord did not come to lock away or "seal up" the prophetic visions as if to hide them; rather, those visions that were long ago unclear and "sealed shut," He took away the seals that lay upon them, opening and unfolding them, handing over the true meaning of the divine Scriptures to His disciples. 

» Hence, it says: "Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah has prevailed, and He will open the seals that lie upon the book," according to the Revelation of John <note>Revelation 5:5.</note>. And what seals are these, if not the obscurities of the prophets? These Isaiah, knowing very accurately, described: "These words shall be as the words of a sealed book." 

» Therefore, the Christ of God did not come to shut away vision and prophet, but rather to spread them wide and bring them into the light. Hence, Aquila seems more accurate in saying, "to complete vision and prophet." For He did not take them away—"I did not come to destroy the law or the prophets, but to fulfill"—as was spoken by the Savior Himself. For "Christ is the end of the law." And all the prophecies concerning Him remained unfulfilled and incomplete until He arrived and placed the "end" or completion upon all the things previously proclaimed about Him.

» It is also possible for the translation of the Seventy <note>The Septuagint (LXX), the standard Greek translation of the Old Testament used by the early Church.</note> to have a similar meaning in the phrase "to seal vision and prophet." Since "the law and the prophets lasted until John," and from that time, the spirit-borne men among the Jewish nation who proclaimed the prophecies concerning Christ have ceased—those who truly oversaw the visions in the sacred words—as if divine grace were shut away from them and bound as if by seals, they vanished. 

» Therefore, it happens that from that time forward, no prophet is active among them, nor does anyone act as a seer among them; from the times indicated, all these things have ceased down to our own time. To these things he adds:

<meta>This page continues Eusebius’s exposition of Daniel 9:24. Having just discussed the "everlasting righteousness" brought by Christ, he now turns to the phrase "to anoint the Most Holy" (literally, the "Holy of Holies"). He argues that this refers not to the Jewish high priesthood, which ceased with Christ, but to Christ Himself as the ultimate High Priest.</meta>

### PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, Book 8. 241

<margin>,,</margin> "...to anoint the **Holy of Holies**." <note>original: ἅγιον ἁγίων (*hagion hagion*). While this usually refers to the inner sanctuary of the Temple, Eusebius interprets it as a title for a person.</note> This too is immediately evident: that until the times of our Savior, the high priests among the Hebrews were called "Holy of Holies" <note>Eusebius suggests that the high priests were seen as the living embodiment of the sanctuary's holiness.</note> according to the sacred rites performed under the Law of Moses. But from that time on, they have ceased to be so, in accordance with the prophecy. Now, the proclamation of Jacob to Judah <note>Genesis 49:10: "The scepter shall not depart from Judah... until he comes to whom it belongs."</note> indicated the failure of the rulers and leaders of the Jewish nation, according to what was stated before. And since the leadership of the people, of the prophets, and of the priests had long ago been suspended, the Word, consequently setting forth through the aforementioned prophecy the downfall of the rulers and leaders of the Jewish nation at the coming of Christ, now declares through the prophecy at hand the failure of the prophets and the priests who formerly flourished among them. He shows that in this matter, they failed at the appearance of Christ; and the presence of our Savior <margin>,,</margin> confirmed this through His deeds. Since **Aquila** <note>Aquila of Sinope was a 2nd-century translator of the Hebrew Bible into Greek, known for his extremely literal, sometimes awkward translation style.</note> rendered it either as "truly sanctified" or "sanctified," someone might think that the ancient high priest among the Jews is meant, as many priests were subordinate to him and called "holy," while the high priest over all was alone called "Holy of Holies." This superficial understanding is indeed true to an extent. For until the times of our Savior, the successive high priests both led the entire people and continually performed the service of God's worship, in accordance with the liturgy legislated through Moses. But from the times of our Savior, their order was first thrown into confusion, and a little later, it was completely extinguished. I myself, having nowhere found the high priest among the Jews named "Holy of Holies" in the Divine Scripture, believe that in these words only the **Only-begotten Word of God** is indicated, and that He is rightly called worthy of this title. For while some among men have made progress and reached the summit of virtue, it is <margin>,,</margin> enough for them to eventually be called "holy" after participating and sharing in Him of whom we say: "You shall be holy, <margin>,,</margin> for I the Lord am holy" <note>Leviticus 11:44.</note>. But "Holy of Holies" could not properly be the name of a man, but only of the **Beloved Son of the Holy One**, who is proclaimed "Holy of Holies" just as He is "King of Kings" and "Lord of Lords." I reserve this for Him alone, inasmuch as He was anointed differently from those ever anointed with the earthly and manufactured ointment of Moses. "You have <margin>,,</margin> loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the **oil of gladness** <margin>,,</margin> above your companions" <note>Psalm 45:7.</note>. Being thus anointed, He Himself speaks in His own person in **Isaiah**: <margin>,,</margin> "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me" <note>Isaiah 61:1.</note>. Since, therefore, our Savior alone among all who have ever lived is witnessed to have been anointed with a different and spiritual—or rather divine—anointment, He is fittingly named "Holy of Holies" (or as one might say, "High Priest of High Priests") and "Sanctified of the Sanctified," according to the oracle of **Gabriel**. All these things, upon the completion of the **seventy weeks**, find their end at no other time than the years of our Savior’s appearance. Regarding these things, then, the aforementioned Angel gave the Prophet a summary decree that they would thus come to pass; and again he takes up the account concerning the seventy weeks, teaching each part accurately—from where the counting of the times must begin, and to what <margin>,,</margin> specific periods it will reach. He says: "And you shall know and understand: from the <margin>,,</margin> going forth of the word to restore and to build Jerusalem, there shall be seven weeks..."

# EUSEBIUS

"...sixty-two weeks, and it shall return, and the street shall be built, and the wall." <note>This continues the quotation of Daniel 9:25 from the previous page.</note> In these matters, it seems right to me not to hide the interpretation of what has been said regarding these places, but to set it forth as well, as it is appropriate for those who are studious. For "the things of friends are common," <note>A common Greek proverb (*koina ta ton philon*) attributed to Pythagoras and cited by Plato and others.</note> as the saying goes. And just as it is proper to use the good words of others without being ungrateful—neither depriving the fathers of their offspring, nor those planting the seeds of their own sowing—we shall set down the very same words. These are found in the fifth book of the *Chronographies* <note>Africanus (c. 160–240 AD) was the first Christian chronographer, attempting to synchronize biblical and secular history.</note> by **Africanus**, and they proceed in this manner:

"That this refers to the appearance of Christ, who was to manifest after seventy weeks, is clear. For in the time of the Savior, or starting from Him, transgressions are done away with and sins reach their end. Because of the remission, lawlessness is wiped out through atonement for unrighteousness, and everlasting righteousness is proclaimed alongside the Law; vision and prophecy last until **John** <note>Referring to John the Baptist; see Matthew 11:13.</note>, and the Holy of Holies is anointed. For before the appearance of our Savior, these things were only expected, not present.

The angel suggests that the number—that is, the seventy weeks, which is four hundred and ninety years—should begin from the 'going forth of the word' to restore and build Jerusalem. This occurred in the twentieth year of **Artaxerxes**, king of the Persians. <note>Artaxerxes I (reigned 465–424 BC). His 20th year is generally cited as 445 or 444 BC.</note> For **Nehemiah**, his cupbearer, having made a request, received the response that Jerusalem should be rebuilt, and the word went out commanding these things. For until that time, the city had been a wasteland. Although **Cyrus**, after the seventy years of captivity, permitted anyone who wished to return voluntarily, those who went down with the high priest **Joshua** and **Zerubbabel**, and those who followed later with **Ezra**, were prevented from building the Temple and the surrounding wall of the city, as this had not yet been commanded.

Thus, it remained so until Nehemiah and the reign of Artaxerxes, and the one hundred and fifteenth year of the Persian sovereignty. From the capture of Jerusalem, it had been one hundred and seventy-five years. And then King Artaxerxes permitted the city to be built. Nehemiah, having been sent down, completed the work, and the street and the wall were built, as was prophesied. From that point, as we calculate it, seventy weeks are completed reaching to Christ. For if we should begin to count from any other point, the time will not coincide, and many absurdities will follow. 

For if we begin the count of the seventy weeks from Cyrus and the first return, it exceeds the time by more than one hundred years; the time is even greater if we count from the day the angel delivered the prophecy; and much greater still if we count from the beginning of the captivity. For we find the Persian kingdom bounded by two hundred and thirty years, and that of the **Macedonians** <note>The Hellenistic period following Alexander the Great.</note> extending for three hundred and seventy years, and from there to the eighteenth year of **Tiberius Caesar** is sixty years. <note>These figures represent Africanus’s specific chronological system, which differs from modern estimates but aims to make the 490 years fit perfectly.</note> But from Artaxerxes, the seventy weeks are completed reaching to the time of Christ, according to the Jewish method of reckoning. For from Nehemiah, who was sent by Artaxerxes to rebuild Jerusalem in the one hundred and fifteenth year of the Persian kingdom..."

<meta>This page continues Eusebius’s presentation of the chronological argument for the "Seventy Weeks" in Daniel 9. ### EVANGELICAL PROOF, Book 8

> In the twentieth year of the reign of **Artaxerxes** <note>Artaxerxes I Longimanus, King of Persia; his 20th year was approximately 445/444 BC.</note>, which was the fourth year of the eighty-third **Olympiad** <note>The Olympiads were four-year Greek cycles used for dating; the 83rd Olympiad, 4th year, corresponds to 445/444 BC.</note>, until this time—which was the second year of the two-hundred and second Olympiad, and the sixteenth year of the reign of **Tiberius Caesar** <note>Approximately 29/30 AD, the traditional date for the beginning of Christ’s ministry.</note>—the total is four hundred and seventy-five years. This amounts to four hundred and ninety-four <note>original: "ϟδ" (94). In lunar calculations, 475 solar years equal approximately 490 lunar years (the 70 weeks of Daniel); the text here specifies 494, perhaps reflecting a variant calculation or a scribal error for 490.</note> Hebrew years when counted according to the lunar course. This is easily stated: the solar cycle consists of three hundred and sixty-five and a quarter days, while the lunar year consists of three hundred and fifty-four days. The twelve-month lunar year thus differs from the solar by eleven and a quarter days. Because of this, both the Greeks and the Jews insert three intercalary months <note>term: "intercalary months" (ἐμβολίμους μήνας) — extra months added to the calendar periodically to keep the lunar months in sync with the solar seasons.</note> every eight years. For eight times eleven and a quarter makes a three-month period. Therefore, the four hundred and seventy-five solar years result in fifty-nine eight-year cycles plus three months. Since a three-month intercalary period occurs every eight years, this adds fifteen years (short by only a few days). These fifteen years, added to the four hundred and seventy-five years, complete the seventy weeks. Such is the calculation from others.

But if we must also bring forward our own interpretation of these passages, I say that the Word did not divide the seventy weeks at random or by chance. By dividing them into "seven and seven" <note>Usually interpreted as 7 weeks and 62 weeks in most translations of Daniel 9:25.</note>, and then another sixty-two, and then after other events achieved in the interval, adding the one final week, he defined the total number of the seventy weeks. He says, therefore:

> "And you shall know and understand: from the going out of the word to restore and to build **Jerusalem** until **Christ the Prince** <note>original: "χριστοῦ ἡγουμένου" (*christou hegouμένου*). While this refers to the Messiah, Eusebius will soon suggest it also applies to the line of "Anointed Leaders" or High Priests.</note> shall be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks." Then, after bringing in certain other events in the middle, he adds the last week, saying: "And one week shall confirm the covenant for many." I believe it must be admitted by all who attend to the words of God that these things were not sketched out at random nor without divine inspiration.

This, then, seemed to us to be the first point well worth noting, leaving the precise solution of the matter to the readers. But if we must not hide what has occurred to us, I say that there is another sense or interpretation of the "Christ the Prince" mentioned in the passage. This "from the going out of the word to restore and to build Jerusalem until Christ the Prince" refers to nothing other than the succession of **High Priests** who led the people after the prophecy and the return from **Babylon**. It is the custom of the Scripture to call these men "christs" <note>term: "christs" (χριστούς) — literally "anointed ones." In the Old Testament, kings and high priests were anointed with oil, thus becoming "christs."</note>. For they alone held the leadership of the nation, beginning with **Joshua son of Josedek** <note>The first High Priest of the Second Temple, who returned from exile with Zerubbabel.</note>, the High Priest, after the return from Babylon, and continuing until the times of the appearance of our Savior Jesus Christ. I believe, at any rate, that the period of their leadership is what is signified by: "from the going out of the word to restore and to build Jerusalem until Christ the Prince, seven weeks and sixty-two weeks." The "weeks of years" collected into years amount to four hundred and eighty-three <note>69 weeks multiplied by 7 years equals 483 years.</note>. These extend from the reign of **Cyrus** <note>Cyrus the Great, the Persian king who allowed the Jews to return from exile in 538 BC.</note> to the beginning of the Roman rule, when **Pompey**, the Roman general, stood before Jerusalem, took the city by siege, and made the whole nation a subject to the Romans. From that time on, they paid tribute and obeyed Roman commands. Up to this time, then, the number of four hundred and eighty-three years is bounded, at which point also the legal succession [of priests] ceased...

XX.ii.

...the law of succession from the fathers for presiding over the nation, having received the priesthood. I suppose that the divine Scripture, in the present passage, names these as "christs" <note>original: "χριστούς" (christous). Indeed, Josephus the Hebrew <note>referring to the historian Flavius Josephus</note> cited an even longer time for the completion of the outer structures surrounding the temple; thus, for these reasons, it is likely that the first seven weeks, amounting to **forty-nine years**, were set apart according to the word of the prophecy. Having previously established the starting point with Cyrus and Joshua son of Josedech, Eusebius now traces the line through the Hellenistic period, the Maccabean revolt, and the eventual Roman conquest under Pompey, leading up to the reign of Herod the Great.</meta>

->### PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, Book 8<-

...the high priest Eleazar, during whose time the Seventy <note>The "Seventy" refers to the legendary seventy-two Jewish scholars who translated the Hebrew Bible into Greek (the Septuagint) in Alexandria.</note> translated the divine Scriptures and deposited them in the libraries at Alexandria. After him came another Onias, who was succeeded by Simon; it was during his time that Jesus son of Sirach was well known, the man who composed the book called the **All-Virtuous Wisdom** <note>original: "πανάρετον σοφίαν" (panareton sophian). This is the book of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus.</note>. After him, another Onias—bearing the same name as the former—was leader, under whom Antiochus [Epiphanes] besieged the Jews and forced them to adopt Greek customs. After him, Judas, surnamed **Maccabeus** <note>The name "Maccabee" is often thought to mean "The Hammer," referring to Judas's role as a guerrilla leader against the Seleucid Greeks.</note>, took charge of affairs and cleansed the sanctuary of the ungodly. He was succeeded by his brother Jonathan. And then came Simon; it was at his death that the 177th year of the Syrian rule <note>term: "Syrian rule" — This refers to the Seleucid Era, which began in 312 BC. The 177th year corresponds to roughly 135 BC.</note> was reached, and the first book called "Maccabees" concludes its history at this time. 

Thus, from the first year of Cyrus and the Persian kingdom until the end of the Maccabean record and the death of Simon the high priest, 425 years are totaled. After these events, John [Hyrcanus] succeeded to the high priesthood, as Josephus says, for twenty-nine years. After him, Aristobulus ruled for one year; he was the first after the return from Babylon to place a **royal diadem** upon his head in addition to holding the high priesthood. He was succeeded by Alexander, who was both king and high priest, presiding over affairs for twenty-seven years.

Up to his time, the total from the first year of the reign of Cyrus and the return of the Jewish nation from Babylon is 482 years; the first high priest in this line, as we have said, was the one named by the prophecy as an **anointed leader** <note>original: "χριστὸν ἡγούμενον" (christon hegoumenon). Eusebius argues that the "Anointed One" or "Messiah" mentioned in Daniel 9 refers to the line of high priests who were literally anointed with oil.</note>. After these, upon the death of their supreme high priest Alexander, the Jewish nation was threatened by anarchy and disorder, so that their kingdom fell into the hands of a woman <note>This was Queen Salome Alexandra, who ruled from 76 to 67 BC.</note>. When her two sons, Aristobulus and Hyrcanus, fell into strife with one another, Pompey—the Roman general—arrived at Jerusalem. He took the city by siege and defiled the holy places, even entering into the inner sanctuary of the temple. These events occurred in the first year of the 179th Olympiad <note>term: "Olympiad" — An ancient Greek four-year period used for dating. The 1st year of the 179th Olympiad is approximately 63 BC.</note>, 495 years after the reign of Cyrus began (which was in the 55th Olympiad).

At that time, Pompey, having taken control of Jerusalem, sent the aforementioned Aristobulus to Rome in chains and handed the high priesthood to his brother Hyrcanus; from that point on, he made the entire nation subject to the Romans. After him, Herod, the son of Antipater, having killed Hyrcanus, was entrusted with the kingdom of the Jews by the Roman Senate. He was the first **foreigner** <note>original: "ἐξ ἀλλοφύλου γένους" (ex allophylou genous). Herod was an Idumean, not a member of the priestly Hasmonean family, which Eusebius sees as a fulfillment of prophecy regarding the end of the Jewish line of kings.</note> to rule the nation, and he destroyed the established order of the high priests as laid down in the Law of Moses. 

For while the divine Law commanded that the one presiding as high priest should serve God for life, Herod did not grant this service to those of the proper lineage; instead, he gave the succession of high priests to certain obscure and foreign men. Even then, he did not allow them to serve continuously, but granted the honor to different people at different times for a short and fixed period. Thus, the first seven "weeks" are delimited from Cyrus to Darius, and the remaining sixty-two weeks are delimited from Darius to Pompey the Roman general. According to a third way of looking at it, if you simply summarize the times of the seven and the sixty-two weeks, they total 484 years, reaching down to Augustus [himself]...

->### PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, Book 8<-

...this too occurred during the reign of Herod, the first king of a foreign race <note>Herod the Great was Idumean by descent, rather than a member of the Judean priestly or royal lines. This was seen by early Christians as a fulfillment of the prophecy that the "scepter shall not depart from Judah... until he comes to whom it belongs."</note>, under whom the birth of our Savior Jesus Christ is recorded as having taken place. If you take the number we are indicating, starting from the time of Darius and the completion of the Temple, and calculate the progression, you will see the alignment. For in the second year of Darius, the seventy-year period of the desolation of Jerusalem was fulfilled, as the prophet Zechariah indicates, saying:

> On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is Shebat, in the second year of
> Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah son of Berechiah. Then he adds: And the 
> angel of the Lord answered and said, "Lord Almighty, how long will you not have 
> mercy on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, which you have overlooked these 
> seventy years?"

Indeed, Daniel, having observed this time through divine foreknowledge, notes: "I, Daniel, understood in the books the number of the years, concerning which the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, for the completion of the desolation of Jerusalem, seventy years; and I set my face toward the Lord my God, to seek by prayer and supplication." Then, after the prayer, the angel appeared to him and foretold the matters concerning the **seventy weeks** <term>seventy weeks: In Daniel 9, "weeks" refers to "weeks of years," where one week equals seven years. Seventy weeks thus equals 490 years.</term>, signaling the time from which the counting must begin, saying: "And you shall know and understand from the going forth of the word to answer and to build Jerusalem until Christ the leader." 

Now, although a command was given by the word of the Lord for Jerusalem to be rebuilt, the work did not initially proceed because the neighboring peoples prevented it. But after these events, when Darius <note>Darius I, known as Darius the Great (reigned 522–486 BC).</note> gave the order and the construction of the Temple was completed under him, Daniel’s prophecy began to find the start of its fulfillment from that point, where it says: *from the going forth of the word to answer and to build Jerusalem.* 

As he had said: *I, Daniel, understood in the books the number of the years... seventy years.* Thus, in the second year of Darius, the completion of the seventy-year period of desolation is shown to have been reached. Consequently, we must begin our calculation of the seventy weeks from the 66th **Olympiad** <note>An Olympiad is a four-year period used by Greeks to track time. The 66th Olympiad began around 516 BC.</note> and from the second year of Darius, in which the building works were finished. 

If one calculates the subsequent years from this point, they would find that up to the time of Herod himself and the Roman monarch Augustus—under whom the birth of our Savior appeared in this life—there are 483 years. These are the seven and sixty-two weeks <note>7 + 62 = 69 weeks. 69 weeks × 7 years per week = 483 years.</note> set apart according to the prophecy of Daniel. For from the 66th Olympiad to the 186th, there are 121 Olympiads in between, which equals 484 years. This accounts for the current Olympiad, during which time Augustus, the Roman King, in the fifteenth year of his reign, held power over Egypt and the rest of the civilized world. It was by him that Herod, the first foreigner, was entrusted with the kingdom of the Jews. 

Our Savior and Lord, Jesus the Christ, was born under Herod at the very fulfillment of the years of his birth, which was also the completion of the seven and sixty-two weeks in Daniel. After these weeks—which are divided and separated by a long interval from the final remaining week—many other things prophesied to happen in the meantime are fulfilled through the middle of the oracle's prediction, which...

<meta>This page continues Eusebius’s chronological argument that the "Seventy Weeks" prophecy in Daniel 9 predicts the end of the legitimate Jewish High Priesthood and the transition of power to Herod the Great and the Roman Empire, coinciding with the coming of Christ.</meta>

->### PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, Book 8<-

> "The matters concerning him of whom I spoke: after the seven weeks and the sixty-two weeks, the **anointing** <term>anointing: The Greek word *chrisma* refers here to the "Christ-like" office of the High Priest, who was literally 'anointed' with holy oil.</term> shall be destroyed, and there is no judgment in it. And he shall destroy the city and the sanctuary together with the leader who is coming, and they shall be cut off as in a flood, and until the end of a war shortened by desolations."

And these things clearly received their fulfillment during the time of Augustus and Herod, in whose reign we say the aforementioned seven weeks are summed up. For in an orderly and systematic way, the high-priestly anointing lasted until the times of Herod and Augustus; however, the direct succession of the ancient high priests was curtailed after Alexander, the father of Hyrcanus. Herod, having killed Hyrcanus, is said to have no longer entrusted the **liturgy** <note>The "liturgy" refers to the sacred sacrificial duties and public service performed by the High Priest in the Temple.</note> to those who were successors by paternal descent, but instead assigned it to various obscure and insignificant men. Hence the oracle, taking this into account, elaborates by saying:

> "And after the seven weeks and the sixty-two, the anointing shall be destroyed, and there is no judgment in it." The other translators have also clearly rendered this: **Aquila** <note>Aquila of Sinope was a 2nd-century translator who produced an extremely literal Greek version of the Hebrew Bible.</note> says, "And after the seven weeks and the sixty-two, the **anointed one** shall be destroyed, and there is nothing for him." And **Symmachus** <note>Symmachus the Ebionite was another 2nd-century translator known for his more idiomatic and elegant Greek style.</note> says, "And after the seven weeks and the sixty-two, **Christ** shall be cut off, and he shall have nothing." From this it is most clearly established, in my opinion, that the "Anointed Leader" <note>original: *christos hēgoumenos*</note> is the one indicated in our interpretation.

For after the completion of the stated weeks, he says, "the Anointed One shall be destroyed." As I have said, this refers to the one who, by succession from the priestly race, presided over the nation. This succession continued for as long as the weeks were not yet fulfilled. When they reached their end, in accordance with the prophecy, the one who presided over the nation by ancestral succession was "cut off." This was Hyrcanus, whom Herod himself killed, seizing the right to appoint the national ruler so that it no longer belonged to Hyrcanus; for Herod himself was of a foreign race <note>Herod was an Idumean, meaning he was not of the tribe of Levi or the line of David, making him an "alien" king in the eyes of many Judeans.</note>. 

It was not only Hyrcanus—who was an "Anointed One" and the last of the ancient high priests—who was cut off, but the ancestral succession of the ancient high priests was also abolished and corrupted. The very anointing according to the laws was no longer performed according to proper judgment, but in a disordered and confused manner, not according to the legislation of Moses. All these things coincided exactly with the prophecy which said,

> "The anointing shall be destroyed, and there is no judgment in it." Then, fearing that everyone would turn toward Aristobulus, he killed him in Jericho, arranging for him to be drowned while swimming, as we have already shown. After him, he no longer entrusted the high priesthood to the descendants of the Hasmonean sons. Archelaus, his son, acted similarly to Herod regarding the appointment of high priests, as did the Romans after him when they took over the kingdom of the Jews." Again, in other places, he says these things about him: "Herod, having become king, built this citadel in a suitable place..."

# PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, Book 8

" ...When a divine voice <note>original: "φωνῆς ἀθεέας" - likely referring to the account in Josephus, *The Jewish War* 6.5.3, where a supernatural voice in the Temple was heard saying, 'Let us depart hence' just before the destruction.</note> said, 'Let us depart from here.' Philo also bears witness to these same events, saying that Pilate set up the royal standards in the temple by night, and that from that moment an era of rebellions and successive disasters befell the Jews. From that time on, uprisings of all kinds of evils did not cease against the whole nation and their metropolis <note>Jerusalem</note>, until the final war against them and the last siege. In that siege, every kind of destruction flowed together like a flood—famine, plague, and the sword—and all those who had plotted against our Savior were cut off. 

It was then that 'the abomination of desolation' <note>original: "βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως" — a reference to Daniel 9:27 and Matthew 24:15, usually interpreted by early Christians as the Roman presence or idols in the Temple ruins.</note> stood in the temple; it has remained there even until now, growing worse in its desolation every day. It is likely that this will continue until the end of the world, according to the limit declared by the prophecy, which says: 'And until the completion of time, completion shall be given upon the desolation.' <note>Daniel 9:27.</note> This saying was sealed by our Savior and Lord Jesus Christ when He said: 'When you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place, then know that its desolation has come near.' <note>Matthew 24:15.</note> 

If any of those of the circumcision <note>A common early Christian term for the Jewish people.</note> feel shame at these facts, they should be told that they are not only making themselves out to be liars regarding what has clearly and visibly come to pass, but they are also declaring the prophecies to be false, as far as they are concerned. For if the prophecies encompass the whole of time within 'seventy weeks of years,' foretelling what would happen in the interval, and now nearly a thousand years have passed from the time of the prophecy down to us, they cannot show that anything written has failed to happen. This is despite the prophecy predicting the end of their anointing <note>Referring to the end of the High Priesthood and the Davidic line.</note>, the destruction of their city and their sanctuary, and their inhabitants being destroyed and cast out in a flood of war and sudden ruin. 

But what is most miraculous of all is seen even now: I mean the 'abomination of desolation' standing even to this day in what was formerly the Holy Place—the very thing about which our Lord and Savior uttered His finished words. Since these things are still clearly visible before our eyes, one can only marvel that those of the circumcision dare to look such evidence in the face; it is as if they are blinded and darkened in their minds, failing to see such clear and manifest fulfillments of the Divine Scriptures. This has happened to them according to the voice of Isaiah, which was fulfilled in them, when he prophesied: 'In hearing you shall hear and not understand, and seeing you shall see and not perceive. For the heart of this people has grown fat, and their ears are heavy of hearing, and they have closed their eyes, lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn back, and I should heal them.' <note>Isaiah 6:9–10.</note> 

But regarding the Gentiles who have believed in the Christ of God, it was said long ago: 'Those to whom it was not told about Him shall see, and those who have not heard shall understand.' <note>Isaiah 52:15.</note> By His grace and the grace of the Father who sent Him, we have spoken to the best of our ability on these passages, and we arrive at the conclusions we have reached without ignorance...

<summary>Eusebius argues that the physical destruction of Jerusalem and the "Abomination of Desolation" in the Temple are historical fulfillments of Daniel's and Jesus's prophecies. He contrasts the "blindness" of the Jewish people toward these events with the "sight" granted to the Gentiles through faith.</summary>

# EUSEBIUS

The arguments we set out before also possess their own accuracy; therefore, we should employ them as they are soundly established.

-> FROM MICAH <-

The prophet foretells that the signs of the times of the Lord's coming among men shall be as follows: the total destruction of the sacred rites held in honor among the Jews, the recognition of the God proclaimed by the prophets among the nations <note>The "nations" (Greek: *ethne*) refers to the non-Jewish or Gentile world.</note>, and a profound peace among all these nations.

> Hear, all you peoples, and let the earth give heed, and all who are in it; and the Lord shall be a witness among you, the Lord from His holy house. For behold, the Lord is coming out of His place; He will come down and tread upon the high places of the earth. The mountains shall be shaken beneath Him, and the valleys shall melt like wax before the fire, and like water rushing down a steep slope. All this is because of the impiety of Jacob, and because of the sin of the house of Israel. Then, after many other intervening words, he adds, saying: Hear these things, you leaders of the house of Jacob, and the remnants of the house of Israel, who abhor justice and pervert all that is right, who build Zion with blood and Jerusalem with iniquity. Her leaders judged for bribes, her priests gave answers for a fee, and her prophets divined for silver; yet they leaned upon the Lord, saying, "Is the Lord not among us? No evil shall come upon us." Therefore, because of you, Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become like a storehouse for fruit, and the mountain of the house of the Lord shall become a forest grove. And it shall come to pass in the last days that the mountain of the Lord shall be manifest, established upon the peaks of the mountains, and it shall be raised up above the hills. Peoples shall hasten to it, and many nations shall go and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and they will show us His way, and we shall walk in His paths." For out of Zion shall go forth a law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. And He shall judge between many nations, and shall rebuke strong nations even unto a far-off land. They shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into sickles; nation shall no longer lift up sword against nation, nor shall they learn to war anymore. Everyone shall rest beneath his own vine and beneath his own fig tree, and there shall be no one to make them afraid, for the mouth of the Lord Almighty has spoken these things.

We have already examined these passages previously in their proper places. It has been demonstrated how, never before the times of our Savior Jesus Christ’s appearance among men, were the ancient sacred things of the Jews—the mountains called Zion and Jerusalem and the buildings upon them, specifically the Temple, the Holy of Holies, and the Altar, and everything dedicated to the honor of God—seen to be shaken and removed from their place. This happened in accordance with the Word which said: *Behold, the Lord is coming out of His place; He will come down upon the high places of the earth, and the mountains shall be shaken beneath Him.* After these things were shaken, the souls of those "of the circumcision" <note>original: "ἐκ περιτομῆς" — a common New Testament and Patristic term for the Jewish people.</note>—who are here called "valleys" because of their current humiliation—now lament the disappearance of their former heights. They "melt like wax before the fire" and like "water rushing down a slope—" <meta>catchword: -slope [original: σει, part of 'katabasei']</meta>

<summary>Eusebius uses the prophecy of Micah to argue that the destruction of the Jerusalem Temple and the conversion of the Gentiles were divinely foretold events triggered by the coming of Christ. He interprets the "shaking of mountains" as the literal and spiritual displacement of Jewish religious authority.</summary>

### THE PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, Book 8

...due to the multitude of those who currently hold power in them falling into worse states daily. All these things, he says, shall happen because of the impiety of the house of Jacob and the sin of the house of Israel. Following this, he explains through whom this impiety and sin came, saying: 
<margin>”</margin> 
Those who abhor justice and pervert all that is right, who build Zion with blood and Jerusalem with iniquity. 
Among these "bloods" was also that matter of the "evil waters" <note>This likely refers to the "bitter water" of trial or, metaphorically, the guilt of the crucifixion.</note> about which they confessed, drawing that impious cry upon themselves: 
<margin>”</margin> 
"His blood be upon us and upon our children" <note>original: *to haima autou eph’ hēmas kai epi ta tekna hēmōn* — quoting Matthew 27:25.</note>. 
Because of these very things, he says: 
<margin>”</margin> 
Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall be like a lodge for fruit. 
<margin>”</margin> 
Has this ever occurred, or reached its fulfillment, except after the crimes committed against our Savior? Since that time and until now, an extreme desolation has overtaken these places. The sight of their once-famous Temple—instead of the ancient study and practice of the prophetic and divine words which the children of the Hebrews and the God-beloved prophets, priests, and teachers of the whole nation once zealously performed there—is now being farmed by foreign men <note>Eusebius refers to the Roman/pagan inhabitants who took over the land after the Jewish-Roman wars.</note>, no different from the rest of the country. We have seen this with our own eyes: the site being plowed by oxen and sown with seed.

And Jerusalem itself has become like a "lodge for fruit" <note>A temporary hut used by guards of a vineyard, symbolizing something fragile and abandoned.</note>, its ancient harvest having been destroyed; or rather, it has become a "heap of stones," according to the Hebrew reading. Indeed, Aquila <note>A 2nd-century scholar who produced a literal Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible.</note> says: 
<margin>”</margin> 
"For your sake, Zion shall be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall be a heap of stones." 
<margin>”</margin> 
For having been inhabited by foreigners, it is even today "stone-quarried" <term>lithologia</term> <note>The act of gathering or clearing stones; here it refers to the literal dismantling of the ruins for building materials.</note>, as all of us who inhabit the city pick out the stones from its ruins for our private, common, and public buildings. It is a gloomy sight to behold the stones from the Temple itself, and from the once-sacrosanct inner courts, being taken away for the shrines of idols and for the construction of public theaters.

With these events so clearly visible to everyone, the New Law and the Word of the New Covenant of our Savior Jesus Christ must surely be evident from the prophets. Because of this Word, countless multitudes of people and entire nations have abandoned their ancestral gods and their ancient, superstitious errors, calling instead upon the God over all. Therefore, they have been deemed worthy of a profound peace, so that there is no longer a "rule of many" <note>Eusebius refers to the end of warring city-states and small kingdoms, replaced by the centralized Roman Empire.</note> or local kingdoms, nor does nation lift up sword against nation. They no longer spend their time in mutual wars as before, but as the prophecy says: 
<margin>”</margin> 
Each of the farmers rests under his own vine and under his own fig tree, with no one to make them afraid. 
<margin>”</margin> 
These things have never been fulfilled at any other time in history since the world began, except under the supremacy of the Romans from the time of our Savior’s appearance until now. Thus, we have received an undeniable proof that the time of the Lord’s prophesied presence among men has arrived.

" ...the Feast of Tabernacles <term>original: skenopegia; a Jewish autumn festival where participants lived in temporary booths to remember the wilderness wanderings</term>. And it shall be, that whoever does not go up from all the tribes of the earth to Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord Almighty, even upon them shall these [plagues] be added. If the tribe of Egypt does not go up or come there, upon them also shall be the fall with which the Lord shall strike all the nations of the earth, as many as do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles. This shall be the sin of Egypt and the sin of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles."

Zechariah prophesied these things after the return from Babylon while Darius was reigning, at a time when Jerusalem was just then being rebuilt from its former desolation <note>Referring to the destruction of the First Temple by the Babylonians in 586 BCE</note> which it had suffered under the Babylonians. The entire time is calculated from the second year of Darius until the Roman Emperor Augustus, amounting to seven and sixty-two "weeks" of years mentioned in the book of Daniel <note>A total of 69 "weeks" or 483 years; early Christians used this timeline to prove Jesus arrived exactly when the prophets predicted</note>, which comes to four hundred and eighty-three years, as we demonstrated in our previous exercises. 

It was according to Zechariah’s prophecy that the fulfillment of the prophet’s words was established, stretching from the time of the Macedonians under Alexander until Augustus. For when during those times—according to those who speak of God in the prophets—was the Lord seen by men, so that many nations recognized him, confessed him as the only God, fled to him for refuge, and became his people? Or when during the times of the Macedonians did the prophesied king come, riding upon a beast of burden and a young colt? And when was the Jewish nation stripped of its envied name and its royal military order in Jerusalem—its chariots and horses—as its armed forces were destroyed? 

For the oracle indicated this when it said: "Behold, your king comes to you, righteous and saving; he is meek and riding upon a beast of burden and a young colt, and the war bow shall be destroyed." These things were divinely foretold concerning the abolition of the royal status of the Jewish nation. Following this, the promise of peace for the nations is given, in harmony with what was granted before: that there would be an abundance of peace from the nations. In place of this, Aquila <note>A 2nd-century scholar famous for his literal Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible</note> and the other translators have rendered it: "and he shall speak peace to the nations." 

This was most especially established and literally fulfilled during the reign of Augustus, when all polyarchy <term>The rule of many different local kings or chieftains</term> was abolished and peace took hold of most of the inhabited world. For who before the Roman times—under the Persians or the Macedonians—was such a King of the Jews that his rule extended from sea to sea, and from the rivers to the ends of the earth? 

For this is how the other translators have made it clear. Aquila, at least, says: "and he shall speak peace to the nations, and his authority shall be from sea [to sea], and from the river unto the ends of the earth." This agrees with what is said in the seventy-first Psalm concerning the Christ who was to be hymned from the seed of Solomon: "In his days righteousness shall arise, and abundance of peace, until the moon be taken away; and he shall have dominion from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth." While these things are said regarding Solomon, they fall in no way short of the things spoken in the prophet. Let anyone who wishes explain when or how or in what times these things occurred, or when at any time after the Babylonian siege did a second—

-># THE PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, Book 8<-

<page-num>255</page-num>
<header>PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, Book 8</header>

> ...the <term>Feast of Tabernacles</term> <note>original: "Skenopegia"; a Jewish harvest festival where people lived in temporary booths to remember the wilderness wanderings.</note>. And it shall be, that as many as do not go up from all the tribes of the earth to Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord Almighty, even these shall be added to those others. And if the tribe of Egypt does not go up, nor come there, upon them shall be the fall with which the Lord shall strike all the nations of the earth, as many as do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles. This shall be the sin of Egypt, and the sin of all the nations, as many as do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.

These things Zechariah prophesied after the return from Babylon, while Darius was reigning, at the very time when Jerusalem was being raised up from its former desolation which it had suffered under the Babylonians. The total time calculated from Darius the Persian until Augustus, the Roman Emperor, comes to seven and sixty-two <term>weeks of years</term> <note>These are "prophetic weeks" where each "day" represents a year, a system found in the Book of Daniel.</note>, which are mentioned in Daniel; these make four hundred and eighty-three years, as we demonstrated in our recent studies, during which Zechariah prophesied. From the time of the Macedonians, starting with Alexander and continuing until the end of Augustus's reign, the events recorded in the prophetic words are established as having been fulfilled. 

For when else during those times did the Lord, who is spoken of by the prophets as God, visit men, so that many nations recognized him, confessed him alone as God, fled to him for refuge, and became his people? Or when during the earlier times of the Macedonians did the prophesied King come, riding upon a beast of burden and a young colt? Or when did he utterly destroy the "chariots and horses" <note>symbolizing military power</note> called from Ephraim and the royal battle-array of Jerusalem itself, and cast down the weaponry of the Jewish nation? For this is what the oracle indicated when it said: 

> "Behold, your King comes to you, righteous and bringing salvation; he is meek and riding upon a beast of burden and a young colt, and the war bow shall be destroyed." 

These things were always prophesied concerning the removal of the royal dignity of the Jewish nation, after which, conversely, the theme of peace among the nations is added, in harmony with what was previously granted: "and an abundance of peace from the nations." Instead of this, <term>Aquila</term> <note>A 2nd-century scholar who translated the Hebrew Bible into very literal Greek.</note> and the other translators have rendered it: "and he shall speak peace to the nations." 

This is especially established as having been fulfilled literally starting from the reign of Augustus; from that time, every "rule of many" <note>original: "polyarchia"; referring to the various local kings and warring factions.</note> was abolished, and peace took hold of the greater part of the inhabited world. But before the Roman times, during the Persian or Macedonian eras, what Jewish king ever existed of such a kind that he ruled "from sea to sea, and from the rivers to the ends of the earth"?

> For this is what the other translators have shown. Aquila, for instance, says: "And he shall speak peace to the nations, and his power shall be from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the world." 

With this agrees what is said in the seventy-first Psalm <note>Psalm 72 in modern Bibles.</note> concerning the Christ who was to be born from the seed of Solomon, though it was never fulfilled in Solomon: "In his days righteousness shall arise, and an abundance of peace, until the moon is taken away; and he shall rule from sea to sea, and from the rivers to the ends of the world." To say these things refer to the son of Solomon falls short of the prophetic words. When, therefore, and how, or in what times did these things happen? Let anyone who wishes explain it, or let them say when at any time after the second Babylonian siege these things took place.

<sig>Yy.ii.</sig>

# PROOF OF THE GOSPEL, BOOK 8
### Yy.iii.

...nations that fought against Jerusalem, did he range himself among them? Or when did his feet stand upon the Mount of Olives? Or when did the Lord become King over all the earth, himself the one Lord over all men, with his name encircling the whole earth and the desert? For one could never show these things to have been brought to fulfillment at any time prior to the Roman period—during which times their Temple underwent a second manifestation <note>original: "emphasmon." Eusebius refers here to the Temple's visibility or its state of being "brought to light" through its final destruction and the subsequent events.</note> of ruin, after the one by the Babylonians—and since that time until now the city has been inhabited by people of every nation. It is also demonstrated that our Lord and Savior, Jesus the Christ of God, made his own dwelling-places upon the mountain over against Jerusalem, fulfilling the word which says: *And his feet shall stand upon the Mount of Olives which is opposite Jerusalem.* <note>Zechariah 14:4. Eusebius interprets this literally through Jesus’s presence on the mountain (the site of the Ascension and the Olivet Discourse) and spiritually through the spread of the Church.</note> This is because, through the divine beauty of the Church’s structure built throughout the whole inhabited world, all the nations—according to the prophecy—celebrate the <term>Feast of Tabernacles</term> <note>original: "Skenopegia," the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Eusebius reinterprets the "pitching of tents" as the establishment of Christian churches.</note> in every place to the God of the prophets. Leading a life of purification from that time onward, they have "pitched their tents" in every city and land. These would be the local Churches of Christ. For the powers of our Savior Jesus Christ pitched these "tents"—which are far superior to the tents of Moses—throughout the whole inhabited world, so that every man and all the nations might perform the Feast of Tabernacles to the God over all. Since, therefore, we see these things which were long ago proclaimed to the nations receiving their fulfillment in our own time, as well as the events of Hadrian’s time <note>Referring to the Roman Emperor Hadrian, who crushed the Bar Kokhba revolt (132–135 AD), renamed Jerusalem "Aelia Capitolina," and forbade Jews from entering.</note> and the things proclaimed against the Jewish nation because of him—namely the burning of the Temple and their final desolation, which even today can be seen with one’s own eyes just as the prophecies foretold—what is left to say? Only this: to confess that the prophesied King, the Christ of God, has come, and that the fulfillment of the signs regarding his presence has clearly taken place in each of the ways demonstrated.

And Egyptians shall rise up against Egyptians, and a man shall fight against his brother, and a man against his neighbor. City shall rise against city, and law against law; and the spirit of the Egyptians shall be troubled within them, and I will scatter their counsel. And they shall consult their gods, and their images, and those who speak from the belly <note>original: "engastrimythous," meaning ventriloquists or spirit-mediums.</note>, and those who speak from the earth. (And after many other things spoken in riddles, he adds:) In that day there shall be an altar to the Lord in the land of Egypt, and a pillar at its border to the Lord. And it shall be for a sign forever to the Lord in the land of Egypt; for they shall cry to the Lord because of those who afflict them, and the Lord shall send them a man who shall save them; judging, he shall save them. And the Lord shall be known to the Egyptians, and the Egyptians shall know the Lord...

He then introduces Isaiah 19 as a prophecy of Christ's "coming to Egypt" and the conversion of its people.</summary>

# OF EUSEBIUS THE PAMPHILIAN
### [Book 6, Chapter 20]

> ...God in 그날, and they shall perform sacrifices, and shall make vows to the Lord, and shall perform them. <note>Isaiah 19:21. Eusebius is continuing a citation from the previous page.</note>

And these things we have already explained in part. If, then, we do not see the Egyptians—having abandoned their ancestral gods—calling upon the God of the prophets as we do; if an altar has not been raised throughout all Egypt, in every place, city, and countryside, to the God spoken of solely by the Hebrews; if the "handmade idols" of Egypt have not been shaken, their demonic power having failed and the ancient superstition having been lifted from the souls of the Egyptians; and if, in addition to these things, the civil war among the Egyptians has not been silenced in every city and every house—wherein some accepted the Lord and the worship of the God of the prophets, turning away from the age-old error of many gods, while others still clung to the ancestral evil of idols and fought against those who accepted the Lord; if even now, when they attempt to consult their own gods, their statues, their <term>mediums</term> <note>original: "eggastrimythous," literally "belly-talkers" or ventriloquists, used in the Septuagint to describe those who summon spirits of the dead.</note> who speak from the earth, and their spirit-talkers, they find this refuge to be unfulfilling and useless because the demons are no longer able to act as they once did; if all these things are not shown to have reached their fulfillment in actual deeds, then let no one think that the prophetic oracle has been fulfilled, nor that the Master and Lord has visited the life of men.

But if the inhabitants of Egypt are seen even now—by their very deeds, which are far clearer than any words—to be of two minds, with some recognizing the God of the prophets and abandoning their ancestral gods for His sake, while others remain in a state of rebellion; and while the latter still call upon their gods, their statues, and those who speak from the earth (who are able to do nothing), the former have established an altar to the Lord of the prophets and a church in every city throughout the whole land of Egypt; and if in their tribulations and the persecutions against them they no longer call upon beasts, or the creeping things of the earth as gods, nor upon wild animals and irrational creatures as their ancestors did, but call upon the God over all, and have received the fear of Him alone into their minds, performing vows to Him which are no longer for demons, and fulfilling promises worthy of God—how does it not follow that we must confess that the results of these events have already passed into actual fact?

These things were to happen because of the Lord’s arrival in Egypt—not in a bodiless form, but by means of a "light cloud," or rather, through the <term>density of the flesh</term> <note>original: "pachous sarkos." Eusebius interprets the "light cloud" of Isaiah 19:1 as a metaphor for the human body of Christ, which "veils" his divinity but allows him to enter the human sphere.</note>. For this is what the Hebrew text contains, hinting at His incarnate presence. As the passage continues, it refers to this very person as a "man savior," saying:

> And the Lord shall send them a man, who shall save them. <note>Isaiah 19:20. The Septuagint Greek uses "man" (anthropos).</note>

Furthermore, the Hebrew text <note>original: "Hebraikon." Eusebius often compares the Greek Septuagint with the Hebrew original or other Greek versions like Aquila or Symmachus.</note> in this place says:

> And the Lord shall send them a savior who shall save them.

Since these things provide such a clear demonstration, I believe the times in which the arrival of the Lord among men was promised have also become plain. These few points have been noted regarding the times of the Lord’s appearance among men. One might find even more by examining the rest of the Divine Scriptures at leisure. However, being satisfied with what has been said, let us now move on to the remaining prophecies, through which we shall discuss the divine work accomplished among men in accordance with the divine predictions.

### Preface.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'T' within a rectangular frame featuring elaborate floral and foliate scrollwork, with a small face or mask at the bottom center.</image-desc>

What then remains after these things, other than to follow our proposed plan and narrate the <term>dispensation</term> <note>original: "oikonomēthenta," referring to the divine plan or "economy" of God’s interaction with humanity through the Incarnation.</note> of the Word of God becoming man? Regarding this subject, we have labored through the previous eight books, sometimes examining the <term>theology</term> <note>original: "theologian," which in Eusebius’s time specifically meant the study of Christ’s divine nature as the eternal Word.</note> concerning Him, and at other times considering His descent from heaven to us, including both the symbolic types and the name, as well as the timing of His arrival. Since these things have been demonstrated, it is now time to look closely at the events of His appearance and to examine how each of these was foretold among the Hebrews. Then, the fulfillment of the prophecy will be confirmed through the sacred <term>mystagogy</term> <note>The teaching or initiation into the mysteries of the faith, here referring to the Gospels.</note> of the Gospels and the historical outcome of the events recorded through them. First of all, then, since all the matters concerning His birth—His lineage, tribe, and seed—have been demonstrated, let us look at the things concerning the new and strange star that appeared at His birth, which was different from the usual stars; for this also was recorded long ago in the time of Moses, intentionally presented as a symbolic type.

Regarding this prophecy, he says that the successors of Balaam were moved by it. For it was likely preserved among them as a notable sign. When it happened that a certain star—strange and unlike the usual ones—appeared in the sky, hanging, as one might say, directly overhead and vertically over Judea, they made haste to reach Palestine. > » saying: Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea, in the days of Herod the

Such is the account in the Holy Gospel. It is worth considering together what the word of the prophecy says would happen at the appearance of the star and the birth of our Savior Jesus Christ: the crushing of the leaders of Moab, the plundering of the sons of Seth, and the inheritance of the rest of the enemies of the Jewish nation, which were Edom and Esau. Has this not already begun through these events—specifically, the pulling down of the <term>invisible rulers</term> <note>original: "aoratōn archontōn," referring to spiritual principalities or demonic powers that Eusebius believed governed pagan nations.</note>, the very demons who were formerly treated as gods by the most ignorant people? Why did he mention no others? It was because of the idolatry of Israel that occurred in the desert, when the people were initiated into the rites of <term>Beelphegor</term> <note>original: "Beelphegōr." Also known as Baal-Peor, a local deity of the Moabites whose worship involved ritual immorality.</note>; this was a demon honored as a god by Balak, the king of Moab. Therefore, since Israel had been conquered at that time by the invisible rulers

> » of Moab—I mean the gods recognized by the Moabites. Indeed, they committed 
> » idolatry and worshiped carved images, as the Scripture says, and they were 
> » initiated to Beelphegor, a demon of the Moabites, at which time they were also 
> » inflamed with passion for the daughters of Moab. It is fitting then that Balaam 
> » prophesies what was to come in the future: the change in their offerings 
> » through the Son. He says, "A star shall rise out of Jacob, and a man shall 
> » rise out of Israel, and shall crush the leaders of Moab."

It is as if he were saying more clearly: the demons of the Moabites, who boasted greatly against Israel, would at the birth of the one prophesied eventually suffer a crushing for all ages. Once they are crushed, the "sons of Seth" and "Edom" and "Esau" and the rest of the nations—who I believe are signified by these names—those who were long ago enslaved to demonic delusion, will be changed from their superstition and become the property of the one prophesied. For he says, "Edom shall be an inheritance, and 

> » Esau his enemy shall be an inheritance."

> » who is his Father: "Ask of me, and I will give you the nations for your inheritance." <note>Psalm 2:8.</note>
